title: isDirty check sorts categories in place, silently flipping the saved primary category
problem: In the isDirty useMemo (MemoryForm.tsx:425), the dirty check calls `formData.categories?.sort()` and `(memory.categories || ...).sort()`. Array.prototype.sort() mutates IN PLACE, and `formData.categories` is the live React-state array reference. This useMemo recomputes on every render (every keystroke, since `formData` is a dep), so the user's chosen category order is silently re-sorted alphabetically inside state. On save (lines 503-506), `categories = formData.categories` (the now-sorted array) is persisted and `primaryCategory = categories[0]` is written to the legacy `category` column. getPrimaryCategory() (memoryCategoryHelper.ts:16) returns `categories[0]` for display/stats/Aiya context. Confirmed scenario: user multi-selects [success, love] intending 'success' primary; the mutation reorders to alphabetical [love, success], so the memory persists with primary 'love' and shows the wrong primary category in lists/stats/export with no user action explaining it.
recommendation: Sort copies, never the live arrays: `[...(formData.categories ?? [])].sort()` and `[...(memory.categories || (memory.category ? [memory.category] : ['uncategorized']))].sort()`.
notes: VERIFIED REAL against current code. The mutation, the state-reference aliasing, and the save path (categories[0] -> primaryCategory -> getPrimaryCategory display) all confirmed. Genuinely user-visible data corruption (wrong primary category) with no user-facing cause. Severity high is justified: it silently changes saved data. Note in practice the user must have multi-selected in non-alphabetical order for it to bite, which is common but not universal, so impact is real but conditional.

title: PDF/CSV export writes raw English enum keys for category and lifeArea while headers are localized
problem: exportToPDF (exportService.ts:98,100) and exportToCSV (135,139) push raw `m.category` and `m.lifeArea` enum values ('gratitude','personal','work') into rows, while column headers use i18n.t('exportCategory') etc. Localized labels DO exist as flat dotted keys ('categories.gratitude' at i18n.ts:341, 'lifeAreas.personal' at i18n.ts:393, both tr and en sets verified). So a Turkish user exporting CSV/PDF gets Turkish headers but English raw enum values in the Kategori/Yasam Alani columns - a half-translated report showing values the user never sees in the app UI.
recommendation: Localize before output: `i18n.t('categories.' + m.category)` and `i18n.t('lifeAreas.' + m.lifeArea)` in both exporters, matching how the UI renders them.
notes: VERIFIED REAL. Raw enum values confirmed at the cited lines; localized dotted keys confirmed present for both categories and lifeAreas in tr and en. Cosmetic/correctness issue in an exported artifact, not a crash, so medium is fair. Note the PDF also only exports the legacy single m.category, not the multi-category array, but that is pre-existing and out of scope of the claim.

title: getBadges/getAchievements ignore the passed memories and re-fetch for streak, causing redundant DB reads and possible inconsistency
problem: getBadges (gamificationService.ts:31) and getAchievements (151) both call `streakService.calculateStreak(userId)` WITHOUT passing the in-hand `memories` array, even though calculateStreak now accepts an optional `existingMemories` param (streakService.ts:19) and otherwise does a fresh `memoryService.getAll(userId)` Dexie read. Achievements.tsx:24-27 runs both in parallel, so each page load does two extra full-table reads the caller already had. Count-based badges use the PASSED array while streak badges use a SEPARATELY fetched array, so if the two snapshots diverge the user could see inconsistent state.
recommendation: Pass the loaded array through: `streakService.calculateStreak(userId, memories)` in both methods so streak and counts derive from one snapshot and the duplicate reads disappear.
notes: VERIFIED REAL but severity lowered from medium to low. The redundant Dexie reads and the dual-snapshot path are confirmed (and the existingMemories param already exists, making the fix a one-word change). However the consistency divergence is largely theoretical: Achievements.tsx passes the same `memories` prop and the Dexie read happens microseconds later; a user racing a just-created memory into one read but not the other on the Achievements screen is an extreme edge case. Main concrete benefit is removing two full-table reads per load. Low.

title: Photo upload retry only fires on thrown errors, but Supabase storage.upload resolves with {error} instead of rejecting
problem: The upload (photoStorageService.ts:77-92) is `retry(() => withTimeout(Promise.resolve(supabase.storage.from(bucket).upload(...)), 30000), { maxAttempts:3, retryable: isNetworkError||isTransientError })`. The Supabase storage client resolves with `{ data:null, error }` on 5xx/transient failures rather than throwing, so the resolved value carries the error past retry to line 94 `if (uploadRes.error)` which throws only after all attempts are spent. isTransientError (retry.ts:84) inspects `error.status` and is only ever invoked in retry's catch path, so a transient 5xx storage failure never triggers the advertised 3-attempt backoff - only raw network throws and the 30s timeout do. Symptom: a momentary storage hiccup that one retry would clear instead fails the upload, leaving base64 inline until the next 5-minute sync poll.
recommendation: Throw inside the retried closure when the result has an error: `const r = await supabase.storage...upload(...); if (r.error) throw r.error; return r`, so retryable(isTransientError) can act; handle the final thrown error after retry exhausts.
notes: VERIFIED REAL. Supabase storage upload's resolve-with-error contract is accurate and the retryable predicate genuinely only runs in the catch path, so storage-side 5xx/429 never retries here. Real but lowered to low: the failure is not silent (it throws and is logged), the memory is not lost (base64 retained, re-synced on the 5-minute poll), and network-level failures + timeout still do retry. So the practical user impact is a slightly delayed photo upload on transient storage errors, not data loss.

title: Aiya profile build is fed history without the user's latest message
problem: In handleSend, `history` (Aiya.tsx:906) is read from chatsRef.current and is deliberately the prior turns only (the appended userMsg has not yet propagated to the ref). After a successful reply, `void maybeUpdateProfile([...history, aiyaMsg])` (line 971) concatenates prior history + Aiya's reply but OMITS the current user message (userMsg, defined at line 890, in scope). The periodic AI profile summary is therefore built from a transcript missing every user turn that immediately preceded a profile rebuild, and the messageCount the cadence relies on is one user turn short, weakening the personalization the profile is meant to capture.
recommendation: Include the user message: `void maybeUpdateProfile([...history, userMsg, aiyaMsg])`.
notes: VERIFIED REAL. history is the pre-userMsg snapshot (confirmed via the ref-read comment at lines 903-906), userMsg is in scope at line 890, and line 971 omits it. Correct, low impact: it only degrades the quality of an internal AI-generated profile summary, with no user-visible breakage. Trivial one-token fix.

title: Suggestion-chip recent-memories window parses date-only strings as UTC, drifting the 7-day cutoff
problem: SuggestionChips computes `recentMemories = memories.filter(m => new Date(m.date) >= oneWeekAgo)` (Aiya.tsx:193). Memory.date is a bare YYYY-MM-DD string, and `new Date('2026-06-20')` parses at UTC midnight - the exact drift parseLocalDate was added to avoid elsewhere (used in streakService.ts:45,71). oneWeekAgo here is a local-now-minus-7-days Date, so comparing a UTC-parsed date against it can flip a memory to the wrong side of the boundary in negative-UTC zones or near the cutoff. Only affects which suggestion chip shows.
recommendation: Use parseLocalDate(m.date) for the comparison and compare against a local-midnight cutoff, consistent with streakService.
notes: VERIFIED REAL. The raw `new Date(m.date)` on a date-only string is present at line 193 and is the same UTC-parse class the rest of the app avoids via parseLocalDate. Genuinely low impact: it only nudges which non-essential suggestion chip appears by at most a day at the boundary; no data or core-flow effect. Keep as a low-severity consistency fix.

title: A future-dated memory keeps the streak flagged active
problem: `daysSinceEnd = round((today - lastStreakEnd)/day)` and `isActive = daysSinceEnd <= 1` (streakService.ts:72,74). If the most recent memory carries a future calendar date, lastStreakEnd is in the future, daysSinceEnd is negative, which still satisfies `<= 1`, so the streak counts as active and currentStreak is reported despite a gap to today.
recommendation: Clamp to the non-future side: `isActive = daysSinceEnd >= 0 && daysSinceEnd <= 1`, and/or drop future-dated memories when building uniqueDates.
notes: VERIFIED REAL in the streak logic itself, but the trigger is largely guarded: validateDate (used in MemoryForm.validateForm and surfaced as the i18n 'dateCannotBeFuture' error) rejects future dates on the AddMemory/edit path, so a user cannot normally save a future-dated memory through the UI. The remaining exposure is device-clock skew (memory.date computed from a fast local clock) or imported/synced data. So the bug is real and the fix is a correct, trivial robustness clamp, but real-world reachability is narrow -> low severity.

title: MemoryForm wipes Layout's Android back-button handler on unmount, leaving back navigation broken
problem: setBackButtonHandler (capacitor.ts:345-352) is a single global slot, not a stack. Layout registers its handler in an effect with deps [handleBackButton] (Layout.tsx:33-36); handleBackButton is stable (navigate is stable) so the effect runs ONCE on mount. MemoryForm registers its own handler on mount and its cleanup calls setBackButtonHandler(null) on unmount (MemoryForm.tsx:668-675). Crucially, AddMemory (the primary 'add a memory' route, AddMemory.tsx) renders MemoryForm under Layout's Outlet while Layout stays mounted. After the user opens Add Memory once and closes it (navigate(-1)), the global handler is null and Layout's effect never re-runs to restore it. Same clobber happens with the Vault/Home modal usage. So on every Android user, after their first add-memory, Layout's intended 'always go home on back' behavior is lost for the rest of the Layout's lifetime.
recommendation: Make setBackButtonHandler maintain a push/pop stack so MemoryForm's cleanup pops back to Layout's handler, OR have Layout re-register its handler on a location/focus effect. Audit every other caller of setBackButtonHandler for the same single-slot clobber.
notes: CONFIRMED with a correction to the original report: back navigation is NOT fully dead. When the handler is null, the native backButton listener in capacitor.ts:376-393 falls through to window.history.back() (or exitApp at the root). So back still does *something*, but it no longer follows Layout's designed navigate('/',{replace:true}) — it walks the history stack instead of always returning home. Real, broad-impact regression on the core add-memory flow; kept high but severity could be argued medium given the history.back fallback softens it.

title: Vault 'Load more' count not reset on filter/search change
problem: displayCount starts at 20 and is only increased by handleLoadMore (Vault.tsx:35,184-190); it is never reset when the active filter/search changes. After a user loads more (e.g. displayCount=80) and then changes category/search, the stale large count persists, so a new filter view that should 'start from the top of 20' instead shows up to 80 items. The slice and the 'Load more' visibility both key off filteredMemories.length (VaultMemoryList.tsx:97,112), so the list never shows MORE than exist and the remaining-count text stays numerically correct — making this a consistency/expectation nit rather than a broken state.
recommendation: Reset displayCount to 20 in an effect keyed on the filter inputs (debouncedSearchQuery, selectedCategory, selectedLifeArea, sortBy, dateRange, searchConnections) or on filteredMemories identity change, so each new filter view starts paginated from the top.
notes: CONFIRMED the missing reset, but the original report's claimed harm is overstated. Because both the slice (slice(0,displayCount)) and the Load-More guard (memories.length > displayCount) use the live filteredMemories array, the UI is self-correcting in both directions — it never hides results that should be loadable nor shows a wrong remaining count. Real but cosmetic; downgraded high->low.

title: Aiya suggestion chip can fire two messages / double-charge on a brand-new chat
problem: handleChip (Aiya.tsx:1000-1013) with no active chat creates a chat then defers send via setTimeout(() => handleSend(text, id), 50). handleSend's guard is `if (!text || sending) return` (line 880), but `sending` is captured from the handleSend useCallback closure (memoized at render), not read live. showChips requires input.length===0 and messages.length===0 (line 1186), both still true during the 50ms window, so the chip row stays visible/tappable. A double-tap (or two different chips) queues two timers that both fire before either setSending(true) commits; both reference the same handleSend closure where sending===false, so neither bails. Result: two user bubbles appended to the same new chat and two metered Aiya requests consumed.
recommendation: Set sending=true (or a queuedSend ref) synchronously in handleChip before scheduling the timer, and/or disable SuggestionChips while a send is pending. Better: have handleChip call handleSend(text, id) directly without the 50ms timer (it already passes the explicit chat id, so no stale-closure dependency on activeChatId remains).
notes: CONFIRMED. The stale-closure on `sending` is the crux: because both timer callbacks share one memoized handleSend whose captured `sending` is false, the guard cannot stop the second call. Window is only ~50ms but a deliberate double-tap or two-chip tap reliably hits it, and the cost (extra metered request) is user-visible.

title: Home 'Need support' resolves and setState/toast after navigating away
problem: handleNeedSupport (Home.tsx:238-275) awaits a ~2.2s breathing promise, then unconditionally runs setRandomMemory/setLastShownMemoryId/setIsBreathing, hapticFeedback('success') and showSuccess(t('foundBeautifulMemory')) (lines 266-274). There is no mounted/cancelled guard around the post-await block. If the user taps 'Need support' then navigates to another tab before the timer elapses, the breath timer still resolves; the setState calls hit an unmounted component and, more visibly, a 'found a beautiful memory' success toast fires app-wide with no memory on screen.
recommendation: Hold an isMounted ref (or AbortController), clear the breath timer on unmount, and bail out of the post-await setState + toast when unmounted. Mirror the cancelled-flag pattern already used by the daily-question effect.
notes: CONFIRMED. React 18 silently no-ops the setState on the unmounted component, so the real user-visible artifact is the spurious global toast (react-hot-toast renders at app root). Low severity — narrow timing window and benign outcome.

title: SettingsSheet 'System' theme is a one-shot snapshot, not a tracked mode
problem: The theme picker offers Light/Dark/System (SettingsSheet.tsx:482-493). 'System' just reads window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)') once and calls handleThemeChange(prefersDark ? 'dark' : 'light'). The store only persists 'light'|'dark' (useStore.ts), so the choice collapses to a concrete value. Consequences a user hits: (1) the System button never renders as selected — its className is hardcoded to the unselected border-gray-200 style with no `theme === 'system'` active branch (lines 482-493), so even right after tapping it looks unchosen; (2) the app does not follow later OS light/dark changes (e.g. at sunset), defeating the option's purpose.
recommendation: Persist a three-way preference ('light'|'dark'|'system'); when 'system', subscribe to matchMedia change events to re-apply the resolved theme; reflect 'system' selection in the button's active state.
notes: CONFIRMED. The System button has no active-state branch at all (verified lines 482-493 use a static unselected className), and the OS-change tracking is genuinely absent because the store has no 'system' mode. Real, label-violating UX gap; medium is fair though it's a feature-completeness issue rather than a crash.

title: Rapid theme toggles can revert via uncancelled 300ms cloud refetch
problem: handleThemeChange (SettingsSheet.tsx:138-166) applies theme locally, then schedules a per-call setTimeout(300) that is never stored in a ref or cancelled. Each call independently UPDATEs the DB then re-SELECTs the full user row and setUser(mapUserFromSupabase(userData)). Tapping light then dark within ~300ms fires two timers; if the FIRST (now-stale) round-trip resolves last, its setUser snaps the UI back to the older theme. The full-row refetch+setUser also clobbers any other user fields changed in the meantime.
recommendation: Hold the timer in a ref and clear it on each call (true debounce); send only the theme update; avoid the full-row refetch+setUser on a simple theme write (merge just the theme field, or skip refetch entirely).
notes: CONFIRMED. Requires rapid toggling within the 300ms window plus unfavorable network ordering, so low severity — but the uncancelled per-call timer and full-object setUser stomp are both genuinely present in the code.

title: Statistics charts and PDF/CSV export read only the deprecated single category, undercounting multi-category memories
problem: MemoryForm writes a multi-select categories[] array (MemoryForm.tsx:503-506, 1124-1142) and the Memory type marks category as deprecated (types/index.ts:8-9). Statistics builds the Category Distribution pie purely from the single m.category: categoryCount[m.category]++ (Statistics.tsx:107-109). A memory tagged [love, fun] only counts toward category[0]=love; the 'fun' tag never appears. exportService does the same in PDF (m.category, exportService.ts:98) and CSV (m.category, exportService.ts:136). The Vault category filter is also single-category-only (useMemoryFilters.ts:94, m.category === selectedCategory), so filtering by a secondary tag misses those memories. Net effect: the category breakdown and any category-based filtering is silently under-reported whenever a user multi-tags.
recommendation: Aggregate over m.categories ?? [m.category] in Statistics (incrementing every category in the array), join m.categories in the export rows, and consider matching against categories[] in the Vault category filter. Fall back to category only when categories is empty/undefined.
notes: VERIFIED REAL. Confirmed MemoryForm.tsx:503-506 builds and persists categories[]; Statistics.tsx:107-109 and exportService.ts:98,136 read only m.category. Also found the same single-category limitation in useMemoryFilters.ts:94 (Vault filter), which strengthens the finding. Severity lowered from high to medium: the totals are not corrupted/NaN, the pie still renders correctly for the primary category, and the deprecated single category is always populated (memoryService.ts:101 ensures categories[]; primary always = categories[0]). Impact is under-counting of secondary tags, a real but non-breaking correctness gap.

title: Statistics avgIntensity/intensity chart can NaN on a null or out-of-range cloud intensity (category/lifeArea portion already handled by the mapper)
problem: The category and lifeArea NaN scenario described in the original finding is NOT reachable: mapSupabaseToMemory coerces every cloud value through toCategory()/toLifeArea() (memoryService.ts:100,108), which fall back to 'uncategorized' for any null/unknown string (memoryService.ts:18-23). Since 'uncategorized' is a key in both categoryCount (Statistics.tsx:97) and lifeAreaCount (Statistics.tsx:117), categoryCount[m.category]++ / lifeAreaCount[m.lifeArea]++ can never hit an undefined key. HOWEVER intensity is NOT normalized on the cloud read path: mapSupabaseToMemory passes intensity: row.intensity raw with no default/clamp (memoryService.ts:102). A legacy/corrupted row with null or out-of-range intensity therefore flows into avgIntensity = sum + m.intensity (Statistics.tsx:92 -> 'NaN/10' on the card) and intensityCount[m.intensity]++ (Statistics.tsx:161-163) creating a stray bucket the 1..10 loop never initialized.
recommendation: Normalize intensity in mapSupabaseToMemory (e.g. clamp Number(row.intensity) to 1-10 with a sane default like 5, matching mapMemoryToSupabase which already uses intensity ?? 5 on write). Additionally guard the avg sum to skip non-finite intensities.
notes: PARTIALLY REAL — original finding overstated. The category/lifeArea crash claim is FALSE (mapper guards via toCategory/toLifeArea at memoryService.ts:18-23,100,108). Only the intensity sub-claim survives, and it is low severity: the write path already defaults intensity (mapMemoryToSupabase memoryService.ts:67) and the create/edit form validates 1-10, so this only triggers on pre-existing malformed cloud rows. Kept as a real low-severity hardening item, downgraded from high to low and re-scoped to intensity only.

title: MemoryCard shows '-N gün önce' for a future-dated memory
problem: getRelativeTime computes diffDays = floor((today - date)/day) (MemoryCard.tsx:39-40) then for diffDays < 7 returns t('daysAgo', { count: diffDays }) (line 44). The daysAgo string is a bare interpolation '{{count}} gün önce' / '{{count}} days ago' (i18n.ts:1103,2209), so a future-dated memory (negative diffDays, e.g. -5) renders '-5 gün önce' / '-5 days ago'. The absolute-date fallback (line 46) is never reached because -5 < 7 is true.
recommendation: Handle diffDays < 0 before the diffDays < 7 branch — show the formatted absolute date (the existing fallback) or a 'today'/future label.
notes: VERIFIED REAL. Confirmed MemoryCard.tsx:39-44 logic and i18n.ts:1103/2209 plain interpolation. Severity lowered medium->low: the form's validateDate blocks future dates on save (formValidation.ts:121-126), so this only manifests for memories imported/synced from another device with clock skew or a future date set out-of-band. Cosmetic, no data loss.

title: MemoryCard / Home render 'null/10' when intensity is missing from cloud data
problem: The intensity badge renders {memory.intensity}/10 with no guard (MemoryCard.tsx:279), and the same raw render appears in Home's random-memory card ({randomMemory.intensity}/10, Home.tsx:588) and the on-this-day list ({memory.intensity}/10, Home.tsx:861). intensity is typed number but mapSupabaseToMemory does not default it (memoryService.ts:102, intensity: row.intensity), so a null/legacy cloud row renders 'null/10'.
recommendation: Best fixed at the source: clamp/default intensity in mapSupabaseToMemory (same root cause as the Statistics intensity issue). Alternatively default at render with (memory.intensity ?? 5).
notes: VERIFIED REAL but low. Same root cause as the intensity half of stats-bad-category-intensity-bucket: cloud read path (memoryService.ts:102) is the only place intensity can arrive null/invalid; write path and form validation prevent it for app-created memories. Confirmed the unguarded renders at MemoryCard.tsx:279, Home.tsx:588 and Home.tsx:861. Severity lowered medium->low (cosmetic, narrow trigger).

title: MemoryForm detail panel shows the date one day off in negative-UTC timezones
problem: The date row formats the chosen date with new Date(formData.date).toLocaleDateString(...) (MemoryForm.tsx:1162-1165). formData.date is a bare 'YYYY-MM-DD' string, which new Date() parses as UTC midnight; in a timezone behind UTC that renders the previous calendar day. The rest of the app deliberately uses parseLocalDate to avoid exactly this (Statistics.tsx:149, useMemoryFilters.ts:76-83, Connections.tsx:55, and memoryService.ts:106 keeps the bare date string for the same reason). So a US-timezone user picks 'June 21' and this row alone displays 'June 20', contradicting the picker and the saved card.
recommendation: Format via parseLocalDate(formData.date).toLocaleDateString(...) (or a formatMemoryDate helper) so the displayed day matches the stored local date, consistent with the rest of the app.
notes: VERIFIED REAL. Confirmed MemoryForm.tsx:1162 uses new Date(formData.date) while every other date consumer uses parseLocalDate. This is a genuine inconsistency the prior timezone pass missed in this one spot. Kept at medium — user-visible and confusing, but display-only (saved value is correct).

title: Vault 'Load more' window is not reset when filters/search change
problem: displayCount is local state initialized to 20 and only grows via handleLoadMore (Vault.tsx:35,184-190); it is never reset when filteredMemories changes. After a user expands the list (e.g. displayCount=200) and then switches to a different filter that matches many memories, the list immediately renders up to 200 rows instead of the initial 20-row page, so the lazy 'page' no longer corresponds to the new filter. Note the original finding's 'hides results' claim is FALSE: VaultMemoryList slices memories.slice(0, displayCount) (VaultMemoryList.tsx:97) which clamps, so narrowing the filter never hides matches and never crashes.
recommendation: Reset displayCount to 20 in a useEffect keyed on searchQuery/selectedCategory/selectedLifeArea/dateRange/searchConnections/sortBy, so each new filter starts from the initial page size.
notes: PARTIALLY REAL. Confirmed displayCount is never reset (Vault.tsx) and the slice clamps (VaultMemoryList.tsx:97), so the dramatic 'results hidden' scenario does not occur. The remaining real issue is a minor lazy-loading inconsistency (filter change can show far more than one page). Downgraded medium->low; type kept as ux.

title: Connections sort/search uses host default locale, mis-ordering Turkish names (İ/ı)
problem: Connection list sorting uses a.name.localeCompare(b.name, undefined, { sensitivity: 'base' }) with an undefined locale (Connections.tsx:64), and filtering uses toLocaleLowerCase() with no locale (lines 67,69). With undefined locale the runtime falls back to the host/device locale, not the app's selected tr/en. For Turkish names the dotted/dotless I (İ/ı vs I/i) then sorts and case-folds incorrectly when the device locale differs from the app language, so visually-similar connections sort apart and a case-insensitive search can miss entries.
recommendation: Pass the active i18n.language explicitly to localeCompare and toLocaleLowerCase ('tr' / 'en') so ordering and search match the app language.
notes: VERIFIED REAL but low. Confirmed Connections.tsx:64,67,69 omit the locale argument. Real edge case for Turkish users on non-tr devices, but cosmetic/ordering only; the count-based primary sort (line 63) dominates so name ordering is a secondary tiebreak. Low severity.

title: Memory text has no maximum length; long pastes grow the textarea unbounded with no counter
problem: The textarea has no maxLength attribute (MemoryForm.tsx:863-879) and validateMemoryText only enforces a minimum (validateMemoryText(formData.text, 10), MemoryForm.tsx:457; formValidation.ts:91-105 has no upper bound). autoResize sets height to scrollHeight with only a floor (Math.max(scrollHeight, 120), MemoryForm.tsx:446) and no max-height, so a very long paste grows the textarea to thousands of pixels inside the modal, and the full blob is persisted to draft storage. There is no character counter or upper limit feedback.
recommendation: Add an upper-bound check to validateMemoryText (with an i18n error + a visible counter as the limit approaches) and cap textarea growth with a max-height + internal scroll.
notes: VERIFIED REAL but low. Confirmed no maxLength on the textarea (MemoryForm.tsx:863-879), no upper bound in validateMemoryText (formValidation.ts:91-105), and uncapped autoResize (MemoryForm.tsx:442-447). Edge-case/ergonomics polish rather than a functional bug; kept type ux, low severity.

title: Abandoned/failed sync items have no proactive, ambient surfacing — user believes memories are backed up
problem: syncAll marks items 'abandoned' after 10 attempts (memoryService.ts:312-314), on a corrupt payload (356) or repeated crash (280-285), and getSyncStatus reports an 'abandoned' count (671-696). The original claim that 'nothing reads getSyncStatus' is FALSE: SettingsSheet.handleSync (lines 277-289) calls getSyncStatus and folds abandoned+failed into a user-visible toast after a MANUAL sync. However that surfacing is only reachable if the user deliberately opens Settings and taps Sync. There is no ambient/passive indication on normal app use: memorySyncService.safeSyncNow (24-38) logs background sync failures at 'warning' and App.tsx never renders any persistent backup-status indicator. So a user on a flaky connection whose create silently becomes 'abandoned' still gets zero unsolicited warning; the memory shows locally and is lost on reinstall/device-switch. The user-impacting gap is real but narrower than reported, hence medium not high.
recommendation: Add an ambient backup-health cue (e.g. a small badge/banner when getSyncStatus().abandoned>0) so the user does not have to open Settings and tap Sync to discover lost backups; and log abandonment at 'error' rather than 'warning' in safeSyncNow.
notes: Severity lowered high->medium: the reported 'nothing reads getSyncStatus / user has zero indication' is partly handled — SettingsSheet surfaces failed+abandoned counts on manual sync. Genuine remaining gap is the lack of PROACTIVE surfacing. Verified against SettingsSheet.tsx:277-294 and memoryService.ts:671-696.

title: OAuth 60s safety timeout could fire a spurious error toast while a slow code exchange still completes
problem: In handleOAuthLogin's native browser-fallback branch a 60s timer (useOAuth.ts:339-345) calls toast.error(t('oauthError')) whenever loadingRef.current is still true. processCallback clears loadingRef on success (137-138) and the timer checks the SAME ref instance, so the common warm path is safe. The residual race the finding describes is real but very narrow: if the deep link arrives but supabase.auth.exchangeCodeForSession (132) is still in flight at exactly the 60s mark on a very slow network, the timer sees loadingRef still true (it is only cleared at line 137 AFTER the await resolves) and shows a red 'login failed' toast moments before the session actually lands. The timer is never cancelled by processCallback. Cold-start is unaffected (handler closure is dead). This is an edge-of-edge timing case, hence low.
recommendation: Before showing the timeout error, re-check supabase.auth.getSession() and suppress the toast if a session now exists; or store the timer id and clear it at the top of processCallback when a code/token is present.
notes: isReal:true but severity medium->low. The primary safe paths the finding itself concedes; only the >60s-in-flight-exchange window produces the bug. Confirmed loadingRef is cleared only after the await at 132, so the window genuinely exists.

title: Oversized photos are never validated/rejected at capture; a >10MB photo fails upload on every sync attempt until abandoned, with no localized feedback
problem: ensureRemotePhotoUrls throws a hardcoded Turkish rate-limit string (photoStorageService.ts:54) and a hardcoded English 'Photo size exceeds maximum limit of 10MB' (69-71). uploadLocalPhotos in memoryService (35-40) catches these, logs at 'warning', and returns the inline refs; the sync loop then re-attempts. MemoryForm.handlePhotoUpload (607-652) only compresses (compressImage 1280px/0.7, line 628) — it never checks the resulting size, so there is NO client-side guarantee a result is <10MB. A memory with an oversized photo will fail upload every sync attempt purely on size, burn the abandonment budget, and the user is never told the photo was too large (the throw is swallowed to 'warning' and the message is not an i18n key). Confirmed: no size check anywhere in the capture path.
recommendation: After compressImage in handlePhotoUpload, check the produced data-URL/blob size and reject or re-compress >10MB with a localized toast; convert the size/rate-limit messages in photoStorageService to i18n keys; and treat a hard size failure as non-retryable so it does not consume the 10-attempt budget.
notes: Verified true. handlePhotoUpload has zero size validation; photoStorageService messages are hardcoded non-i18n strings. Severity medium is appropriate — real data-loss-by-abandonment path plus a hardcoded-string/i18n violation of project rule 2.5.

title: Sending an Aiya message with no connectivity gives only a generic post-timeout error; no pre-flight offline check
problem: handleSend (Aiya.tsx:878-997) does no navigator.onLine pre-check (verified lines 878-902): it optimistically adds the user bubble, sets sending=true, and awaits aiyaService.sendMessage. On no connectivity this rejects, is mapped to t('aiyaNetworkError') (980), the bubble is rolled back and text restored (986-993). So a user with no signal types a message, watches the typing dots for up to the timeout, then gets a red error with no offline-specific explanation. The global OfflineIndicator only reacts to the online/offline browser events / isOnline store flag (OfflineIndicator.tsx:39-47) and will not catch a 'connected but requests failing' stale connection. The rollback is reasonable; the missing piece is an immediate, offline-aware cue and an inline retry affordance.
recommendation: In handleSend, if !navigator.onLine, show an immediate localized offline note and keep the draft without starting the spinner; on a network-class failure attach an inline 'offline — tap to retry' on the rolled-back message rather than only restoring text to the input.
notes: Verified: no pre-flight offline check in handleSend; OfflineIndicator is event-driven and won't fire on stale connections. Genuine UX gap, medium severity stands.

title: MemoryForm save awaits the local create/update with no timeout — a hung IndexedDB write spins the Save button forever
problem: handleSave (MemoryForm.tsx:490-605) sets setSaving(true) at 497 and awaits memoryService.create/update (509/523) with NO withTimeout wrapper. memoryService.create (144-171) does db.memories.add + addToSyncQueue; update (173-199) does db.memories.put + addToSyncQueue. If IndexedDB is wedged (another tab holding a versionchange transaction, WebView/private-mode quota stalls that hang rather than throw), the await never settles, the finally (601-604) never runs, and the Save button shows its spinner indefinitely with no error and no recovery short of killing the app. Network paths elsewhere use withTimeout; the local write path does not. The secondary 500ms/700ms timing concern in the title is cosmetic, but the core hung-write claim is valid.
recommendation: Wrap the create/update await in withTimeout (e.g. 10s) so a hung local write surfaces t('saveErrorRetry') via the existing catch and re-enables the button.
notes: Verified: no withTimeout around the local writes; finally only runs once the await settles. Real (if rare) hang. Severity medium retained. The first clause of the title about a 700ms delay is a distraction; the substantive bug is the missing timeout.

title: Aiya cloud chat-load failure is indistinguishable from 'no chats' — a transient failure on a new device shows an empty list with no retry
problem: aiyaService.loadChats returns null on ANY failure (catch at aiyaService.ts:665-670) AND when there is no data, with no way to distinguish 'failed' from 'empty'. In Aiya.tsx loadData (619-631) a null cloudChats is treated as 'no cloud chats' and the code proceeds with local data only (mergedFromCloud stays null at 631). So a logged-in user on a fresh device whose chats query transiently fails (RLS hiccup, 5xx, expired token mid-request) sees an empty chat list with no spinner, error, or retry, and may assume conversations were lost. Confirmed. Impact is bounded (chats are not lost, only not shown this session; a later successful load recovers them), hence low.
recommendation: Make loadChats return a discriminated result (or throw) so loadData can show a non-blocking 'couldn't load your conversations — retry' affordance, and retry the cloud load on next focus/online.
notes: Verified true at aiyaService.ts:649-670 and Aiya.tsx:619-631. Severity low is correct — data is not destroyed, just not surfaced; lower user impact than the sync-abandonment findings.

title: Session-restore fetchUserData timeout silently downgrades a valid session into an apparent logged-out state
problem: In initializeApp (App.tsx:84-119) getSession is wrapped in a 10s timeout and fetchUserData/ensureUserExists in an 8s timeout. On a fetchUserData timeout the catch (115-119) only console.errors in DEV; setUser is never called, so a user with a genuinely valid persisted Supabase session is rendered logged-out. There is a PARTIAL recovery: onAuthStateChange fires INITIAL_SESSION with the session and the branch at 180-194 (else if session?.user) retries fetchUserData — but if that retry also times out (same slow network / cold Supabase), setUser is again never called and there is no backoff, no minimal-user-from-session fallback, and no 'reconnecting' indicator. A returning user on a quiet session can be left staring at the logged-out UI despite being authenticated.
recommendation: On a restore-fetch timeout where session.user clearly exists, seed a minimal user from the session (id/email) to keep the logged-in shell while data finishes, and/or retry with backoff plus a soft 'reconnecting' indicator instead of silently appearing logged out.
notes: Verified: timeout catch (115-119) never sets user; INITIAL_SESSION path (180-194) gives a partial retry but no fallback/backoff. Severity medium retained — the INITIAL_SESSION retry mitigates the common case but the persistent-slowness case is a real, confusing logout-appearance.

title: useMemories load-error toast has no id, so persistent Dexie failures stack duplicate identical toasts
problem: useMemories.loadMemories calls toast.error(tRef.current('memoriesLoadError')) with no id (useMemories.ts:60). The hook autoLoads on mount (70-74) and refreshMemories re-runs loadMemories. If Dexie reads fail persistently (corrupt DB, quota), every mount / refresh fires another identical toast and react-hot-toast only de-dupes when an explicit id is supplied, so several copies of the same message stack. Verified exactly as described.
recommendation: Pass a stable id: toast.error(msg, { id: 'memories-load-error' }) so repeated failures collapse into one toast.
notes: Verified true and exact. Low severity / trivial fix — only manifests under persistent read failure, but the fix is a one-liner and the analysis is correct.

title: Abandoned sync items can never be re-activated by the user — even manual Sync skips them
problem: syncAll only selects status 'pending' or 'failed' for draining (memoryService.ts:299-305); 'abandoned' items are excluded and no code path ever resets an abandoned item back to pending. memorySyncService exposes only start/stop/syncNow. Crucially, the manual Settings Sync button (SettingsSheet.tsx:260-309) calls memoryService.syncAll directly, which means even an explicit user-initiated Sync will NOT retry abandoned items — it only reports their count via getSyncStatus. So a user whose backups got abandoned during an outage has no in-app action that retries them after connectivity returns; the only recovery is editing each memory to enqueue a fresh 'update'. The reclassified-as-failed items ARE retried (good), but truly-abandoned items are stuck. This is the actionability counterpart to AF-1 and is real.
recommendation: Add a 'retry backups now' action that resets abandoned/failed items (attemptCount=0, status='pending', nextAttemptAt=now) then calls syncNow, wired to the Settings sync button and/or the AF-1 status cue.
notes: Verified true. The finding's premise that abandoned items are excluded (299-305) and never reactivated is correct, and I additionally confirmed the manual Settings Sync (SettingsSheet.tsx:270) calls syncAll and therefore also skips abandoned items — strengthening the finding. Severity raised low->medium: combined with AF-1 there is genuinely no recovery path for permanently-abandoned backups.

title: Sign-up with email confirmation ON logs the user into a broken, session-less state
problem: In handleSubmit (Login.tsx lines 205-282) the sign-up path branches only on data.user.email_confirmed_at === null, never on whether data.session exists. When the Supabase project has email confirmation enabled, signUp returns a user but NO session. The code still shows the 'verify your email' toast (line 216) and then unconditionally continues: refreshSession() (220) returns nothing, the users upsert (226) runs without auth.uid() and is rejected by RLS (only a DEV console.warn at 243), fetchUserData returns null, and execution falls into the 'create local user object' branch (263-277) which still calls setUser + navigate('/'). The user is dropped onto the authenticated home with no real Supabase session; subsequent server writes fail and on next launch App.tsx finds no session and bounces them out. The 'verify your email' message directly contradicts logging them straight in.
recommendation: After signUp, branch on data.session. If session is null (confirmation required), show the verify-email message and keep the user on the login screen (ideally a 'check your inbox' state with the resend button); do NOT setUser/navigate. Only run the upsert/fetch/navigate path when a real session is present.
notes: Confirmed against current code. The whole signUp block (213-278) has zero reference to data.session; it gates entirely on email_confirmed_at. Severity lowered from critical to high: it only manifests when email confirmation is enabled on the Supabase project (a config-dependent condition), but when it is, every new sign-up is affected and lands in a corrupt state, which is a serious first-run failure.

title: Two identical 'Account created, verify your email' toasts on every sign-up
problem: On a sign-up where email is unconfirmed, t('accountCreated') ('Account created! Please verify your email.') is fired twice: once at line 216 immediately after signUp, and again at line 252 after fetchUserData succeeds. Both use duration 6000ms, so the user sees the same message stacked twice for 6 seconds, which reads as a glitch.
recommendation: Show the verify-email toast exactly once. (If the deadend fix above is applied so the non-session path returns early, the line-252 duplicate becomes unreachable anyway — remove it.)
notes: Verified: both line 216 and line 252 fire toast.success(t('accountCreated')) under the same email_confirmed_at === null condition. The duplicate at 252 only fires when fetchedUser is truthy.

title: Resend-verification handler exists but is never reachable, so a stuck unverified user has no way out
problem: handleResendVerification (Login.tsx 112-136, with its own i18n strings verificationEmailSent/failedToSendEmail confirmed present in both tr and en) is fully implemented but never rendered or invoked anywhere in the component — grep finds no JSX wiring it to any button. A user who signs up and never receives (or loses) the confirmation email gets 'email not confirmed' on next login (handled via authErrorMessage) and has no resend affordance and no 'check your inbox' state. They are dead-ended with no self-service recovery.
recommendation: Render a 'resend confirmation email' action — e.g. when signInWithPassword fails with an email-not-confirmed error, or in a post-signup 'check your inbox' state — wired to the existing handleResendVerification.
notes: Verified: handler exists at 112-136; the only buttons in the form are forgot-password (483), submit (496), OAuth, and the signup/login toggle (519). Nothing calls handleResendVerification. i18n keys confirmed at i18n.ts lines 169-170 and 1301-1302. Severity lowered high->medium: it is a genuine recovery gap, but the impact is bounded to unverified users who lose their email, and Supabase resends a verification on a repeated signUp in some configs.

title: Inline forgot-password modal has no Escape key, focus trap, or scroll lock (the proper component is unused)
problem: Login.tsx reimplements the forgot-password dialog inline (538-605) instead of using ForgotPasswordForm, which is never imported (grep confirms no import anywhere in src). The inline version does NOT call useModalPresence, so unlike every other modal standardized by the a11y pass it does not lock body scroll or register an open modal; it also has no Escape-to-close (only backdrop click / Cancel) and no focus trap (Tab escapes to the login form behind it). The unused ForgotPasswordForm component, by contrast, already calls useModalPresence (line 24).
recommendation: Replace the inline modal block with the existing ForgotPasswordForm component (already wired with useModalPresence), or add useModalPresence + Escape handling to the inline version; then delete the dead duplicate.
notes: Verified: inline modal at 539-605 has no useModalPresence, no onKeyDown/Escape handler, no focus trap; only onClick backdrop (544) and Cancel (579). ForgotPasswordForm.tsx calls useModalPresence(true) at line 24 but is imported nowhere. This is a real inconsistency with the rest of the app's standardized modal behavior. Note Onboarding.tsx and MigrationPrompt do use useModalPresence, confirming the standard.

title: useLoginForm, LoginHeader and ForgotPasswordForm are all dead code reimplemented inline in Login.tsx
problem: useLoginForm (full form-state + inline-error-map hook), LoginHeader, and ForgotPasswordForm are each exported but imported nowhere in src (grep confirms only their own definitions match). Login.tsx duplicates all of their logic inline: its own calculatePasswordStrength/getStrengthColor/getStrengthText (79-110), its own header (335-345), and its own forgot-password modal (538-605). A side effect of not using useLoginForm is that the login form surfaces errors via transient toasts (one at a time, auto-dismissed) instead of the persistent per-field inline errors the unused hook supports.
recommendation: Either adopt the existing helpers in Login.tsx (gaining inline field errors and modal a11y) or delete the three unused modules to prevent divergence/confusion.
notes: Verified all three are dead: grep across src returns only the definition sites. Reclassified impact as primarily dead-code/bloat; the inline-error-vs-toast point is accurate but is a quality observation, so low severity is correct. This overlaps with the forgot-modal finding (ForgotPasswordForm).

title: Onboarding can never be replayed once dismissed, and 'X' silently counts as completed; flag is device-local, not per-account
problem: Home gates the tour on !hasCompletedOnboarding (Home.tsx 338). Onboarding's X button calls skip() which is just onComplete (Onboarding.tsx 59-61, 80-85), identical to finishing, permanently setting the flag. There is no replay entry anywhere (grep of Profile.tsx for onboarding/intro/tutorial/replay returns nothing). A first-time user who taps the easy-to-hit top-right X never sees the Vault/Aiya/Statistics explanation again. The flag is stored only in localStorage under 'hasCompletedOnboarding' (useStore.ts 123-134), not per-account, so clearing app data or switching devices replays it, while a second account on the same device never sees it.
recommendation: Add a 'Show intro again' / 'Replay tutorial' entry (e.g. in Profile) that resets the flag, and consider keying completion to the user account rather than device localStorage only.
notes: All three sub-claims verified: skip===onComplete, no replay path in Profile, localStorage-only non-per-account flag in setHasCompletedOnboarding.

title: Brand-new user with zero memories lands on a home of empty/disabled cards instead of a focused first-step CTA
problem: After onboarding, a user with no memories sees Home where: the Need Support button is disabled (disabled={isBreathing || memories.length === 0}, line 433) yet still shows a heading t('needSupport') with subtext t('addFirstMemory') (461-463) — confusing copy for someone with nothing; the random-memory inner action is hidden (memories.length > 0 guard, 468); the streak card shows 'add your first memory to start a streak' (821-822); and the 'on this day' card requires memoriesOnThisDay so is absent (842). The only real entry point is the daily-prompt card, but the overall screen reads as a half-broken dashboard of disabled widgets rather than a single clear 'add your first memory' empty state.
recommendation: For the zero-memory case, render a dedicated empty state with one prominent 'Add your first memory' CTA and hide/replace the support, random-memory, and streak cards until at least one memory exists.
notes: Verified: disabled guard at 433, heading+addFirstMemory at 461-463, random-memory guard at 468, streak empty copy at 821-822, onThisDay card gated on memoriesOnThisDay at ~842. The 'half-broken dashboard' framing is fair. Medium effort because it requires designing/wiring a new empty state, not a one-line change.

title: Logged-out users are never redirected to login; they silently use a throwaway local account whose data the migration prompt can permanently delete
problem: There is no auth guard on the '/' routes (App.tsx 235-251 — index/Home and all children render unconditionally). A user with no session is dropped straight into Home operating under a local id (useUserId falls back to getLocalUserId, useUserId.ts 13-15). Nothing on Home indicates they aren't signed in or that entries live only on this device. When they later sign in, App.tsx (160-164) shows MigrationPrompt; choosing onReject sets confirmDelete (App.tsx 57-59), and the second step's onConfirmDelete calls deleteLocalMemories() (61-64, MigrationPrompt.tsx 91-96), permanently wiping everything written while logged out. A first-time user can invest in many entries, sign in expecting them saved, and (if they misread the two-step prompt) destroy them.
recommendation: Surface sign-in state on Home (e.g. a 'Sign in to back up your memories' banner for local-only users) so guest mode is intentional, and make the migration prompt's destructive path safer (keep-by-default wording — note the delete-confirm step's primary button already defaults to 'keep', which is good).
notes: Verified: no ProtectedRoute/guard in App.tsx routes; useUserId falls back to local id; migration delete fork is reachable via onReject->confirmDelete->onConfirmDelete->deleteLocalMemories. Mitigations already present: the confirmDelete step's prominent gradient button is 'migrationKeep' (cancel) and the destructive option is a plain red text button, which already reduces accidental deletion. Kept at medium; the missing sign-in-state indicator is the more impactful half.

title: Sign-up 'I accept the terms' checkbox has no link to any terms or privacy policy
problem: The sign-up flow forces ticking t('acceptTerms') (validated at 195-199) but the label (Login.tsx 470-472) is plain text — 'Şartları kabul ediyorum' / 'I accept the terms' — with no hyperlink to Terms of Service or Privacy Policy. The user is required to accept terms they cannot read. A privacy-policy.html exists at repo root but is not linked here. Poor UX and an app-store/legal risk for an app collecting personal journal data.
recommendation: Make the terms/privacy references in the acceptTerms label actual links to the hosted policy pages.
notes: Verified: label at 470-472 is a plain {t('acceptTerms')} with no anchor. i18n value confirmed as plain text (no embedded link/Trans component). privacy-policy.html exists at repo root per git status.

title: After password reset, success message auto-redirects to '/' after 2s with no user control or account confirmation
problem: On successful updateUser, ResetPassword sets success and after 2000ms navigate('/') (lines 60-61). The success view (95-100) is just a green message with no button and no indication of which account the user is now in. If the recovery session is short-lived, the user can land on the guest/local home rather than a clearly signed-in state. The silent timed redirect also gives a user no control to read the confirmation.
recommendation: Either route to /login with a 'password updated, please sign in' state, or confirm an authenticated session exists before sending to '/'; prefer an explicit button over a timed redirect.
notes: Verified: setTimeout(navigate('/'),2000) at line 61; success block has no actionable control. Note the page does correctly gate the form on sessionReady (recovery session), so in practice a valid recovery flow usually IS authenticated when reaching '/'. Kept low — the 'lands on guest home' scenario is an edge case, but the silent timed redirect with no button is a genuine minor UX nit.

title: Password strength meter implies 8+ chars / mixed case / symbols but only a 6-char minimum is enforced
problem: During sign-up calculatePasswordStrength (80-88) scores length>=6, length>=8, mixed case, digits, and symbols across a 5-bar meter, and the empty-password hint shows t('passwordHint') (415-419). But the only enforced gate is password.length < 6 (line 183). A 6-char all-lowercase password shows a red 'very weak' bar yet is accepted, so the visual feedback implies requirements that aren't enforced — causing either needless friction or false confidence.
recommendation: Align meter with policy: either enforce the stronger criteria the meter implies, or relabel the meter as advisory and keep the hint truthful about the single 6-char minimum.
notes: Verified: strength function rewards 8+/mixed case/digits/symbols (80-88), meter rendered at 396-414, only enforcement is length<6 at 183. The mismatch is real but cosmetic/advisory — strength meters are commonly advisory, so low severity is appropriate.

title: Failed memory load is indistinguishable from "no memories yet" on every list screen
problem: useMemories exposes an `error` state (useMemories.ts:15,32,57-60) but NO consuming page destructures it: Vault.tsx:25, Statistics.tsx:55, Achievements.tsx:14, Connections.tsx:32 and RelationshipSaver.tsx:23 all pull only `{ memories, loading, refreshMemories }`. When memoryService.getAll() throws, the catch sets error, leaves memories=[], flips loading=false, and fires a single transient toast. Every page then renders its zero-data state as if the user genuinely has nothing: Vault.tsx:225 -> VaultEmptyState with hasFilters=false ("add your first memory"), Statistics.tsx:191 -> "Henüz istatistik yok", Achievements (no zero-branch) -> 0/0 bars, Connections.tsx:176 -> "noConnections", RelationshipSaver.tsx:223 -> "noConnections". The persistent UI lies about the data state and offers an "Add memory" CTA instead of "Retry".
recommendation: Destructure `error` from useMemories in each page and, when set, render a distinct error state with a Retry button calling refreshMemories/loadMemories, shown instead of the empty state. Minimum: gate each empty state on `!error`.
notes: Confirmed against current code. Real and the highest-impact finding in this batch. One caveat on severity framing: this is an offline-first Dexie LOCAL read (memoryService.getAll), so failures are corrupt-store / Dexie-open / mapper-exception cases rather than ordinary network blips, making the trigger less frequent than the wording implies. The user-facing harm when it does fire (silent data loss appearance + wrong CTA) is genuinely high, so high severity stands.

title: Vault flashes the full empty state for one frame before the skeleton appears
problem: useMemories initializes loading=false (useMemories.ts:31); loading flips true only inside loadMemories after the first render commits (effect at :70-74). On Vault's first render memories=[] and loading=false, so Vault.tsx:225 (`filteredMemories.length === 0 && !loading`) is briefly true and VaultEmptyState renders, then swaps to the skeleton list once loading becomes true. On a slow device the "No memories yet" archive illustration blinks before skeletons.
recommendation: Initialize `loading` to `true` (or to `autoLoad`) in useMemories so the first paint is the loading/skeleton state, never the empty state.
notes: Confirmed. Cosmetic single-frame flash; affects all pages using the hook, but each already shows a loading branch once loading flips true. Low impact, near-zero-cost fix.

title: Sending an Aiya message while offline gives no proactive offline cue
problem: handleSend (Aiya.tsx:878) has no isOnline guard (the store exposes isOnline, useStore.ts:7,71). Offline, the user types, sends, sees the optimistic bubble + typing dots, then after the fetch fails the bubble is popped (lines 986-992), text restored to the input, and an inline error shown. The composer is never proactively disabled and there is no "Aiya needs a connection" hint before the round-trip is attempted.
recommendation: Read isOnline from the store; when offline, either disable the send button or short-circuit handleSend with a localized "Aiya needs an internet connection" message before attempting the request.
notes: Partially overstated and downgraded medium->low. The error-mapping claim is now WEAK: line 980 matches `network` OR `timeout` OR `failed to fetch` OR `fetch`, and the bare `'fetch'` substring catches the common offline rejection strings ("Failed to fetch", "Network request failed" contains neither 'fetch'? — 'Failed to fetch' does), so most offline failures already map to aiyaNetworkError (i18n.ts:510/1642) rather than the catch-all aiyaError. The remaining real gap is purely the lack of a PROACTIVE offline guard/disabled composer; the post-failure message is already reasonable. Genuine but minor.

title: Statistics renders an all-zero monthly bar chart when all memories predate the last 6 months
problem: The page-level empty state (Statistics.tsx:191) triggers only when memories.length === 0. A user whose memories all fall outside the last 6 months passes that guard and reaches the charts, where the Monthly Trend BarChart (lines 338-346) renders 6 zero-height bars. No "no recent activity" copy, so the chart reads as broken rather than empty-by-range.
recommendation: When stats.monthlyData sums to 0, show a small inline "no activity in the last 6 months" placeholder inside the chart card instead of an empty axis.
notes: Confirmed. Edge case (requires a user with only old memories), genuinely confusing when hit. Low.

title: Vault "Load more" injects a hardcoded 300ms spinner for data already in memory
problem: handleLoadMore (Vault.tsx:184-190) sets isLoadingMore=true then `await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 300))` before bumping displayCount. filteredMemories is fully client-side and VaultMemoryList.tsx:97 just slices it, so this is a fake spinner delaying memories the user already has by 300ms on every tap.
recommendation: Remove the artificial setTimeout and increment displayCount synchronously; keep the spinner for at most one frame if visual continuity is desired.
notes: Confirmed verbatim at Vault.tsx:187. Pure self-inflicted latency on a hot path. Low severity, trivial fix.

title: Connection rename/delete loops sequential updates with only a disabled button and no progress
problem: applyRename (Connections.tsx:82-115) and applyDelete (117-136) iterate every affected memory with `for (const m of affected) { await memoryService.update(...) }` — sequential awaited round-trips. During this only `busy` disables the Save button (line 289) and the icon buttons (lines 223,235); there is no spinner, progress text, or label change. For a heavily-used connection the dialog looks frozen for seconds, inviting a second tap or force-close.
recommendation: Show a spinner/loading label on Save and Delete while busy (swap text to LoadingSpinner + t('saving')), matching VaultMemoryList's load-more button pattern. Optionally Promise.all the updates to cut wall-clock time.
notes: Confirmed. The sequential loop is real and the only feedback is opacity-via-disabled. Medium stands because it scales with connection usage and the most likely target (a frequent connection) is exactly the slowest case.

title: RelationshipSaver share swallows real errors in an empty catch; export has no error handling
problem: handleShare's catch (RelationshipSaver.tsx:150-152) is empty except a comment "// User cancelled or error" — a genuine navigator.share() failure (not an AbortError cancel) produces no toast and no log, so a failed share looks like a no-op. handleExport (165-191) performs Blob/createObjectURL/anchor-click with no try/catch, so any failure is silent. Neither action shows a busy state.
recommendation: In handleShare, distinguish AbortError (ignore) from real errors (toast t('shareError')). Wrap handleExport's blob/anchor logic in try/catch with a localized failure toast.
notes: Confirmed. The empty catch also conflicts with the project's own rule 1.8 (no swallowing errors). Low user impact (share/export are secondary actions and the common AbortError path is correctly ignored), but it is a real silent-failure path.

title: Achievements with zero memories shows 0/0 bars and empty grids instead of a get-started state
problem: Achievements.tsx has no `memories.length === 0` branch (unlike Statistics.tsx:191). A brand-new user lands on "0/0" summary cards (lines 93-95,111-113) with width-0 progress bars, and the badge grid renders all badges in the locked/opacity-60 state with no guidance to add a first memory, so the screen reads as broken/empty rather than aspirational.
recommendation: When memories.length === 0 (and not loading/error), render a dedicated empty state encouraging adding a first memory, consistent with Statistics/VaultEmptyState.
notes: Confirmed: no zero-data branch exists. Debatable — the locked-badge grid is arguably a valid 'aspirational' first-run view since it shows what can be unlocked. Kept as real but low; the 0/0 summary with empty bars is the weak part.

title: Aiya chat list shows the empty "start a chat" hero before cloud-only chats load
problem: The list view keys layout off `chats.length === 0` (Aiya.tsx:1089,1095) and there is no loading branch for the chat list. The load effect (579-734) renders local chats instantly but for a logged-in user on a fresh device with only cloud chats, setChats happens only after `await aiyaService.loadChats(userId)` resolves (line 622), and `loaded` (set in the finally at 727) is NOT used to gate the hero. Until the fetch settles the full centered "Merhaba! Ben Aiya / Sohbet Başlat" hero is shown, then prior conversations pop in below — the user briefly believes they have no history.
recommendation: Gate the empty hero on `loaded` (or a dedicated chats-loading flag) and show a small skeleton/spinner in the list area until the cloud fetch settles when a logged-in user may have remote chats.
notes: Confirmed: `loaded` state exists but the hero/list render at 1086-1177 never references it. Edge case — only logged-in users whose chats aren't in localStorage (new device / cleared storage). Low impact, real.

title: Future days inside the current month look clickable but silently do nothing
problem: Confirmed against current code. Line 454 computes `const isPast = day > today` (misnamed; tests future) and line 455 `const isDisabled = isPast && !isCurrentMonth`. The render-scope `today` (line 331) is `new Date()` at the current instant, so a future day within the displayed month evaluates day>today true but isDisabled false (because isCurrentMonth is true). That cell renders with hover:bg-primary/10 and cursor-pointer (line 473) and is not disabled (line 465). handleDateClick (lines 177-181) sets today to end-of-day (23:59:59.999) and early-returns on date>today, so tapping a same-month future day produces a hover highlight but no selection and no feedback. Future days are only disabled when they fall in trailing next-month cells.
recommendation: Disable any future day regardless of month: normalize an end-of-day today once and set isDisabled = day > today (drop && !isCurrentMonth). Keep handleDateClick's guard using the same normalized value so click and disabled state agree.
notes: Verified lines 331, 454-455, 463-473, and 177-181. The two `today` values (render-scope new Date() vs click-scope end-of-day) plus the !isCurrentMonth qualifier are exactly the inconsistency described. Real, user-reachable (tap a future day in the current month). Genuine medium UX/logic bug.

title: MemoryForm subcomponents (Fields/Actions/Photos/Header/AdvancedFields) are dead code, not used by the live form
problem: Confirmed. A src-wide grep for MemoryFormFields/MemoryFormActions/MemoryFormPhotos/MemoryFormHeader/MemoryFormAdvancedFields returns only their own definitions plus RangeSlider's import inside MemoryFormFields — no consuming import anywhere. MemoryForm.tsx inlines its own implementation and never composes them. These five components ship unused and encode a divergent, stale UX, creating a maintenance trap where edits land in code the user never sees.
recommendation: Delete the five unused MemoryForm* subcomponents (confirm no lazy/dynamic import first), or wire MemoryForm to compose them. Eliminate the divergent second implementation.
notes: Grep confirmed zero consumers. This is genuine dead code / maintainability risk but has no direct end-user impact, so severity is low (downgraded from the dimension's bug framing). Worth keeping as a cleanup item.

title: Auto-saving drafts with base64 photos can exceed localStorage quota and silently lose the draft
problem: Confirmed. Auto-save (lines 276-291) and the Save-as-Draft button (lines 1338-1341) both localStorage.setItem(JSON.stringify({...formData})), and formData.photos are full base64 JPEGs compressed at 1280px/0.7 (compressImage, line 628), up to 5 photos. Several MB of base64 can exceed the ~5MB localStorage origin quota. The auto-save catch (lines 284-286) only console.warns in DEV, so the user keeps typing believing a draft exists when setItem threw QuotaExceededError. The Save-as-Draft catch (lines 1347-1350) shows draftSaveError and (correctly) does NOT call onClose, so the user stays in the form — slightly less severe than the original claim, but the silent auto-save loss remains real.
recommendation: Exclude photos from the persisted draft (store text/intensity/date/connections/categories only, with a note that photos are not drafted), or size-guard and surface an explicit 'draft too large, photos not saved' message. Do not let a thrown quota error leave the user thinking the draft is saved.
notes: Verified lines 276-291, 628, 1338-1350. The auto-save silent-failure is the real risk. Note the original problem statement overstated the Save-as-Draft path (onClose is inside the try, so it isn't reached on error). Adjusted notes accordingly; still medium because the auto-save path silently loses work.

title: Edit Profile sheet discards typed changes with no confirmation on backdrop tap / Escape
problem: Confirmed. Local state for displayName/bio/birthday/location/avatar (lines 31-36) has no dirty-state guard. Backdrop onClick={onClose} (line 208), the X button onClick={onClose} (line 228), and Escape (useEscapeKey calling onClose when !saving, line 42) all close immediately and discard typed input with no prompt. This is inconsistent with MemoryForm's showDirtyConfirm flow. A user editing a long bio who taps outside loses it silently.
recommendation: Track an isDirty flag (compare current fields to the user record) and route backdrop/X/Escape through a confirmation dialog when dirty (reuse the unsaved-changes pattern) instead of calling onClose directly.
notes: Verified lines 31-37, 42, 208, 228. No dirty guard exists. Real and consistent with the stricter pattern already used in MemoryForm. Genuine medium UX gap on a data-entry sheet.

title: Reminder save shows both error and success toasts when notifications are denied, and weekly day is not persisted offline
problem: Both sub-issues confirmed. (1) In handleSaveReminders, when dailyReminderTime is set but permission is denied, toast.error(notificationPermissionDenied) fires (line 208) and the code continues to the cloud update which, on success, fires toast.success(settingsSaved) (line 241). The user sees an error and a success toast for one Save tap — confusing about whether the reminder is active. (2) weeklySummaryDay is only written into the cloud updates object (lines 216-217); state seeds from user.weeklySummaryDay (lines 104-105,126). On the offline/no-Supabase early return (lines 220-223) it shows settingsSaved but never persists the weekly-day choice locally, so it reverts on next open. dailyReminderTime does not have this gap because it is also scheduled locally via notificationService.
recommendation: When permission is denied, suppress or reword the generic settingsSaved success ('saved, but reminders are off until you allow notifications'). Persist weeklySummaryDay to the local store so the offline 'saved' toast is truthful.
notes: Verified lines 195-249 and the grep for weeklySummaryDay (104-105,126,216-217). Both bundled issues are real but each is minor and edge-case (denied permission; offline). Low severity is correct.

title: Editing photos in an existing memory can be treated as not-dirty, allowing silent close without saving
problem: Confirmed. For an existing memory, isDirty (lines 416-430) compares photos only by count: `formData.photos.length !== memory.photos.length` (line 424). Removing one photo and adding a different one (net length unchanged), or replacing a photo, leaves isDirty false. requestClose (lines 654-661) then closes without the unsaved-changes prompt, and since the user never tapped Save, the photo swap is discarded silently.
recommendation: Compare photo contents, not just count — e.g. compare the joined photo arrays or an identity/hash list — so any add/remove/replace that nets the same length still marks the form dirty.
notes: Verified lines 416-430 (line 424 is length-only) and requestClose 654-661. Real edge case: equal-length photo swaps escape the dirty guard. Medium because it can silently lose a user's photo edit.

title: Login surfaces all validation only as transient toasts, with no inline field errors
problem: Confirmed. handleSubmit (lines 173-199) validates email, password length, password match, and terms purely via toast.error + return; the first failing check wins, so the user learns one problem at a time. A grep for border-red / aria-invalid on the inputs found none — there is no inline error state or red-border affordance next to fields. Compared to MemoryForm's inline per-field errors, the account-creation flow gives weaker, easy-to-miss feedback on mobile.
recommendation: Add inline error text and the existing red-border style under each field (email/password/confirm/terms) in addition to or instead of toasts, so users see exactly which field to fix.
notes: Verified lines 173-199 and grep showing all 'error' references are toast/logging, none inline on inputs. Real but a UX-polish improvement, not a defect; low severity is appropriate.

title: TimePicker shows 09:00 as the spinner default even when cleared, implying a value that is not set
problem: Confirmed. State initializes hours=9, minutes=0 (lines 27-28) and is overwritten from value only when value is non-empty (lines 38-46). displayValue on the trigger correctly shows the placeholder when value is empty (line 221). But opening the picker with no value set displays 09:00 in the spinner as if selected, and handleApply (lines 144-149) commits that 09:00 unconditionally. In Settings, a user who opens the daily-reminder picker just to look and taps Apply sets a 9am reminder they never chose.
recommendation: When value is empty, visually distinguish the spinner default (dim it / show a 'no time set' hint) or require an explicit interaction before Apply commits, so 09:00 reads as a placeholder, not a selection.
notes: Verified lines 27-28, 38-46, 144-149, 221. Real but a low-frequency confusion (only when opening with no value and tapping Apply without changing). Low severity correct.

title: RangeSlider (with keyboard + step buttons) is bypassed by MemoryForm's hand-rolled slider, splitting slider UX
problem: Confirmed. MemoryForm implements its own inline intensity slider (lines 922-994) with its own keyboard handler (lines 932-957) and no step-tick tap shortcuts. RangeSlider.tsx is only referenced by MemoryFormFields (itself dead code per the grep), so the polished RangeSlider with step-tick buttons and shared behavior never reaches the live Add-Memory screen. There are two intensity-slider implementations; the one users touch lacks the tappable numeric step shortcuts, and any RangeSlider improvement won't reach users.
recommendation: Either adopt RangeSlider inside MemoryForm for the intensity control (gaining step-tick taps and shared behavior) or remove RangeSlider if the bespoke slider is canonical, so there is a single source of truth.
notes: Verified the inline slider at 922-994 and grep showing RangeSlider's only consumer is the dead MemoryFormFields. Real maintainability/consistency concern, minor user impact (missing step-tick shortcuts). Low severity / quality-class finding.

title: Android back button permanently breaks after opening & closing MemoryForm once
problem: capacitor.ts uses a single-slot global back handler (`let backButtonHandler` at line 345). Layout registers its handler in an effect with deps [handleBackButton] (Layout.tsx:33-36); handleBackButton is a useCallback over the stable `navigate`, so the effect runs once on mount and never re-runs on navigation. MemoryForm (rendered inline on Home via the FAB, presentation='modal') registers its own handler on mount and on unmount calls setBackButtonHandler(null) (MemoryForm.tsx:668-675) instead of restoring Layout's handler. After the user opens the inline MemoryForm once and closes it, the global handler stays null for the rest of the session. From then on every Android hardware-back falls through to capacitor.ts:385 window.history.back(), bypassing Layout's 'sub-page -> Home; Home -> exit app' model. The whole back-navigation contract is dead after the first add-memory.
recommendation: Make the back handler a push/pop stack in capacitor.ts and invoke the top-most handler; MemoryForm/overlays push on mount and pop on unmount so Layout's handler is restored automatically. Alternatively, re-register Layout's handler on every location change so it reclaims the slot after any modal closes.
notes: CONFIRMED. capacitor.ts:345 single slot; setBackButtonHandler at 350-352; back listener at 376-393. Layout.tsx:33-36 effect deps [handleBackButton] (stable -> runs once). MemoryForm.tsx:668-675 cleanup sets null. Home.tsx:911-934 renders MemoryForm inline (modal). MemoryForm only registers when isNative(), so this is native-Android-specific, which matches the claim. This is the root-cause finding that several others depend on.

title: Hardware back in Aiya chat view exits the whole page instead of returning to the chat list
problem: Aiya has an internal view state ('list' | 'chat', Aiya.tsx:370) not backed by the router. The chat header shows a ChevronLeft back button (Aiya.tsx:1194-1200) whose onClick goToList returns to the list. But Aiya never calls setBackButtonHandler anywhere (verified: no occurrence in Aiya.tsx). So while in chat view, hardware back is handled by Layout's handler -> navigate('/', { replace:true }) (Layout.tsx:24-30) and throws the user out to Home instead of back to the chat list. The on-screen back arrow and the hardware back button do different things.
recommendation: While view==='chat', push a back handler that calls goToList() and returns true; pop it when returning to list. Depends on the handler-stack fix in nav-back-handler-null-after-modal so it composes with Layout.
notes: CONFIRMED. grep shows zero setBackButtonHandler usage in Aiya.tsx. view state at 370, goToList at 844-852, ChevronLeft onClick at 1195. Note: if finding nav-back-handler-null-after-modal has already nulled the slot earlier in the session, back instead falls to window.history.back(); either way it does not return to the list. High severity justified: Aiya chat is a primary flow and the mismatch with the visible back arrow is exactly what Android users notice.

title: Hardware back dismisses the underlying page instead of closing open overlays (ImageModal, ActionSheet, ConfirmationDialog)
problem: ImageModal (Escape+backdrop close, ImageModal.tsx:66-70,224), ActionSheet (useEscapeKey, ActionSheet.tsx:20), and ConfirmationDialog (useEscapeKey, ConfirmationDialog.tsx:45) all support Escape/backdrop dismissal but none register an Android back handler. While one is open over e.g. Vault, hardware back is handled by Layout -> navigate('/'), so back navigates to Home and unmounts the underlying page; the overlay vanishes only as a side-effect and the user loses their place in the list. Native Android UX expects back to close the top overlay first.
recommendation: Each overlay should push a back handler on open that calls onClose and returns true, popping it on close. Requires the handler-stack fix from nav-back-handler-null-after-modal so overlays compose with Layout and MemoryForm.
notes: PARTIALLY CONFIRMED. ImageModal/ActionSheet/ConfirmationDialog all exist and register NO back handler (grep confirms). However ConflictDialog.tsx does NOT exist in src/components (Glob returned nothing) -- dropped from the title/files. Severity lowered from high to medium: the overlays DO close (the page unmounting tears them down) and there is no data loss; the harm is losing scroll/list position and a jarring jump to Home, which is annoying but recoverable. Note: after nav-back-handler-null-after-modal nulls the slot, back instead does history.back(), still wrong but in a different way.

title: Cold-launching /add-memory and pressing Save/Close calls navigate(-1) with no history to return to
problem: AddMemory closes and saves via navigate(-1) (AddMemory.tsx:21,23), assuming a prior history entry exists. /add-memory is a real route (App.tsx:247). If entered as the first navigation of the session (PWA shortcut, push tap, or a page refresh while on /add-memory), there is no previous entry, so navigate(-1) is a browser no-op and the user is stuck on the form after saving (no confirmation), or on native may pop out of the WebView.
recommendation: Fall back to an explicit destination: if (window.history.length > 1) navigate(-1); else navigate('/', { replace: true }). Apply to both onClose and onSave.
notes: CONFIRMED as a real edge case. AddMemory.tsx:21,23 use navigate(-1); route exists at App.tsx:247. In normal use it is only reached from Home (Home.tsx:123,134) so history always exists -- the bug only manifests on cold-launch/refresh, which is uncommon. Severity lowered from medium to low to reflect the narrow trigger. Fix is a trivial guard.

title: Aiya options menu can't be closed with Escape and back dismisses the whole page
problem: The Aiya chat options dropdown (Aiya.tsx:1224-1263) is plain showMenu state with a fixed click-catcher backdrop. It does not use useEscapeKey and registers no back handler.
