A keyboard user cannot press Escape to dismiss it, and on Android hardware back while the menu is open navigates away from Aiya (via Layout) instead of just closing the menu. It only closes via backdrop tap or a menu item.
recommendation: Add useEscapeKey(() => setShowMenu(false), showMenu) and, on native, a back handler that closes the menu first. Keep consistent with other overlay close behavior.
notes: CONFIRMED. Menu at 1224-1263, backdrop onClick at 1232 closes it; no Escape handler and no setBackButtonHandler in Aiya.tsx. Low severity is appropriate: small overlay, recoverable via backdrop tap.

title: Pressing Android back while MemoryForm's unsaved-changes confirm is open does nothing
problem: MemoryForm's back handler always calls requestClose() (MemoryForm.tsx:670-672). When the unsaved-changes confirm is already showing (showDirtyConfirm true and the form still dirty), requestClose() re-enters the isDirty branch and calls setShowDirtyConfirm(true) again (MemoryForm.tsx:654-661) -- a no-op. So with the dirty-confirm visible, hardware back appears dead; the user expects back to cancel/dismiss the confirm but nothing happens, so the nested dialog feels stuck.
recommendation: When showDirtyConfirm is true, route the back press to setShowDirtyConfirm(false) (cancel) instead of re-invoking requestClose, so back peels off the top-most layer.
notes: CONFIRMED. requestClose at 654-661 (isDirty -> setShowDirtyConfirm(true)); back handler at 670-672 calls requestCloseRef.current(); dirty confirm rendered at 1279 with backdrop cancel at 1285. Native-only (handler gated by isNative). Low severity: backdrop tap and the dialog's own buttons still work; only the hardware-back affordance is dead.

title: Aiya chat root uses 100dvh, not visualViewport pixels — composer can sit under the Android keyboard
problem: The Aiya screen root is a fixed `height: '100dvh'` flex column (Aiya.tsx:1442) with a flex-1 message list and flex-shrink-0 composer. The component already tracks the true visible height via visualViewport into `viewportHeight` (Aiya.tsx:483-507) and derives `isKeyboardOpen` from it (line 510), but it only uses that boolean to zero the footer's safe-area padding (line 1383); the tracked pixel height is NEVER applied to the root container. ModalShell deliberately drives its panel height from visualViewport pixels (ModalShell.tsx:33-72, 174, 232-233) for exactly this reason: on Android WebView with adjustResize, CSS dvh/vh often does NOT shrink when the IME opens. If dvh stays full, the 100dvh root keeps full height and the composer is pushed below the keyboard. The focus handler only does textarea.scrollIntoView (Aiya.tsx:527-531), which scrolls the inner list, not the off-screen fixed composer.
recommendation: Apply the already-tracked visualViewport pixel height to the root: replace `height: '100dvh'` on Aiya.tsx:1442 with `height: viewportHeight + 'px'`, mirroring ModalShell, so the composer stays pinned above the keyboard.
notes: Verified against current code. The viewportHeight state and visualViewport listeners exist and are functionally identical to ModalShell's useVisualViewport, but the value is never bound to the container's height — only the dvh literal is. This is the highest-impact item: typing is Aiya's primary action and on adjustResize Android WebViews the composer can be hidden behind the IME. Confirmed high.

title: "Double tap to zoom" hint is hover-only and pointer-events-none — never shows on touch
problem: The hint that teaches the core zoom gesture is `opacity-0 hover:opacity-100 transition-opacity pointer-events-none` (ImageModal.tsx:336). Touch devices have no :hover, so on phones — the only place pinch/double-tap zoom matters — the hint is permanently invisible. The pinch/double-tap zoom feature (handleDoubleClick line 109, handleTouchMove pinch line 165) is therefore undiscoverable on mobile; users see a full-screen photo with only close/next/prev and no cue it can be zoomed.
recommendation: Show the hint briefly on open for touch (auto-fade after ~2s on first view via a timer/state) instead of relying on :hover.
notes: Confirmed verbatim at line 336. Genuine discoverability gap for the zoom feature on mobile. Severity medium is fair: it does not break anything, just hides a feature.

title: Swipe navigation tracks finger 0 during a 2-finger pinch — pinch release can flip to the next/prev image
problem: The container wires swipe handlers alongside pinch/pan handlers on the same element (ImageModal.tsx:244-255). useSwipe.onTouchMove records targetTouches[0] on every move with no touch-count guard (useSwipe.ts:24-29) and onTouchEnd fires onSwipeLeft/Right whenever |deltaX|>50 (useSwipe.ts:34-45); those callbacks are wired only when `!isZoomed` (ImageModal.tsx:212-213). During a pinch that begins and ends at scale 1 (user starts to zoom but releases before crossing scale>1, so isZoomed stays false), finger 0 routinely moves >50px horizontally, so lifting the fingers navigates to a different image instead of doing nothing.
recommendation: In useSwipe.onTouchMove abort/cancel the swipe when e.touches.length > 1 (e.g. null out touchStart), so multi-finger gestures never count as a swipe.
notes: Verified: useSwipe has no multitouch guard and ImageModal forwards onTouchMove unconditionally. Real edge case; impact is occasional accidental navigation during a partial pinch. Medium is appropriate.

title: Scroll-down FAB is pinned 100px from bottom and does not react to keyboard — can overlap the composer
problem: The scroll-to-bottom FAB is positioned `bottom: calc(100px + var(--safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px))` (Aiya.tsx:1373) and its offset never reacts to isKeyboardOpen. When the keyboard opens, the composer's safe-area padding is removed (line 1383) and the visible area shrinks, so the round FAB at the bottom-right can float over the textarea/send-button area the user is reaching for.
recommendation: Hide the FAB while isKeyboardOpen, or compute its bottom offset from the composer height so it always clears the input bar.
notes: Confirmed the FAB offset is a static 100px and is not conditioned on isKeyboardOpen. Real but minor and partly entangled with aiya-root-dvh-keyboard (if the root is sized correctly the overlap window narrows). Downgraded from medium to low: the FAB only shows when scrolled up, and tapping it scrolls to bottom anyway.

title: Opening the photo viewer from inside MemoryForm stacks two competing Tab focus traps
problem: MemoryForm renders ImageModal as a child of its content (MemoryForm.tsx:1260-1266) while the form lives inside ModalShell (MemoryForm.tsx:1404-1416). ImageModal is `fixed inset-0` but remains a DOM descendant of ModalShell's panel. ModalShell installs a window-level Tab trap scoped to its panelRef (ModalShell.tsx:139-161) and querySelectors ALL focusables in the panel — which now includes both ImageModal's buttons and the form fields behind it. ImageModal installs its own Tab trap (ImageModal.tsx:74-99). Both fire on the same keydown; because focus inside ImageModal still satisfies ModalShell's `panelRef.contains(active)` check, ModalShell will not exclude the hidden form fields, so Tab can move focus from the viewer onto form fields rendered behind it. useModalPresence (useModalPresence.ts) is only a counter for the bottom nav, so there is no suspension of the parent trap.
recommendation: Suspend ModalShell's focus trap (or mark the panel inert) while a nested modal is open, e.g. via a shared modal-stack signal, so only the topmost trap is active.
notes: Verified both traps exist and there is no suspension mechanism; the conflict is real. Keyboard-only edge case affecting a minority of users who open the photo viewer from the form and Tab; no impact on touch/mouse. Severity confirmed low.

title: Intensity-slider drag can also scroll the modal body because the non-passive touchmove never preventDefaults
problem: The intensity slider registers a document-level touchmove with { passive: false } (MemoryForm.tsx:743) but the handler (onMove → updateSliderFromX, MemoryForm.tsx:711-725, 735-737) never calls e.preventDefault(). The non-passive registration buys the ability to cancel the gesture but it is unused, so while the user drags the thumb the browser can also treat the gesture as vertical scroll, making the scrollable modal body jitter/scroll under the finger and precise value selection awkward on a phone.
recommendation: Call e.preventDefault() inside onMove while isDraggingSlider is true (the listener is already non-passive), so the drag is consumed and the modal body does not scroll.
notes: Confirmed: passive:false is set but no preventDefault anywhere in the move path. Real but minor mobile-ergonomics polish. Low severity is correct.

title: Tapping a non-zoomed photo near its edges can dismiss the viewer because close is on the full-screen backdrop
problem: The outer layer has onClick={onClose} (ImageModal.tsx:224) and the inner container stops propagation only when !isZoomed (lines 236-242). The container is `max-w-4xl w-full max-h-[90dvh]` with p-4 on the outer layer, so on phones the container fills the width (w-full) and most letterboxing around a portrait photo falls INSIDE the container (which stops propagation), not on the backdrop. Real backdrop area is the top/bottom strips outside max-h-[90dvh] and, on wider viewports, the horizontal margins outside max-w-4xl. Tapping those strips closes the viewer.
recommendation: If accidental dismissal is a concern, restrict close-on-tap to the explicit X button (and/or a swipe-down) rather than the whole backdrop.
notes: Partially valid but the original problem overstates phone impact: because the container is w-full, portrait letterbox is mostly inside the close-suppressing container on phones, so the misfire is limited to the top/bottom backdrop strips and to wider (tablet/landscape) viewports. Tap-outside-to-close is also a widely expected modal convention, so this is borderline-by-design. Kept as a real but very low-priority UX nit.

title: English count strings have no singular form: "1 memories", "1 months ago"
problem: Three EN count keys with live call sites render ungrammatical English at count=1. connectionMemoryCount (i18n.ts:1205 '{{count}} memories') is rendered at Connections.tsx:210 with the real per-connection count, so a connection with one memory shows '1 memories'. memoriesOnThisDay (i18n.ts:1545) is rendered at Home.tsx:845 with memoriesOnThisDay.length → '1 memories' in the On-This-Day card. memoriesDeleted (i18n.ts:1266) is rendered at Vault.tsx:115 with selectedMemories.size → '1 memories deleted' when one is deleted. All are routinely reachable with count=1.
recommendation: Add i18next plural variants for these EN keys: connectionMemoryCount_one/_other, memoriesOnThisDay_one/_other, memoriesDeleted_one/_other (e.g. _one: '{{count}} memory'). Add identical _one/_other in TR for parity (TR text is the same for both). The existing days_one/days_other pair (i18n.ts:1582-1583) is the correct model already in the file.
notes: VERIFIED real for connectionMemoryCount, memoriesOnThisDay, memoriesDeleted — all three have live call sites passing real counts that can be 1. CORRECTIONS to the original finding: (1) photosAdded (i18n.ts:1265) is a DEAD key — grep for t('photosAdded') returns zero call sites, so it never renders to a user; dropped from scope. (2) monthsAgo/yearsAgo are NOT broken in practice: Home.tsx:326-333 explicitly branches to oneMonthAgo/oneYearAgo when the value === 1, so monthsAgo/yearsAgo only ever receive count>1. The raw keys are theoretically wrong but unreachable today. Severity lowered high→medium: cosmetic grammar issue, English-only, no functional impact.

title: Missing English key silently renders Turkish to English users (fallbackLng: 'tr')
problem: i18n.ts:2272 sets fallbackLng: 'tr'. If a key is ever missing from the en resource, an English user sees raw Turkish (e.g. 'Kaydet', 'Bir hata oluştu') instead of English. The failure mode for English users (untranslated foreign text) is worse than for Turkish users.
recommendation: Set fallbackLng: 'en' so missing strings degrade to English, which a broader audience can read, while keeping the tr/en parity test as the primary guard.
notes: VERIFIED: fallbackLng:'tr' confirmed at i18n.ts:2272. This is a latent/preventive concern only — the prior pass added a tr/en parity test that guards current keys, so no key is missing today and no user hits this right now. Real but purely defensive; severity lowered medium→low. Many EN strings also carry inline defaultValue fallbacks at call sites, further reducing exposure.

title: Misspelled Turkish word in Aiya suggestion chip: 'Minettarlık' (should be 'Minnettarlık')
problem: i18n.ts:538 aiyaChipGratitude: 'Minettarlık anılarımı göster'. The correct Turkish spelling is 'Minnettarlık' (double n). The chip is a visible tappable suggestion in the Aiya chat UI, so a native Turkish user sees a spelling error on a prominent, polished surface.
recommendation: Fix to 'Minnettarlık anılarımı göster'.
notes: VERIFIED at i18n.ts:538 — text reads exactly 'Minettarlık anılarımı göster'. 'Minnettarlık' is indeed the correct Turkish spelling (double n). Genuine user-visible typo on a primary AI surface. Kept at medium; one-character fix.

title: Conflict resolution dialog formats timestamps in Turkish for all users
problem: ConflictResolutionDialog.tsx:98 hardcodes toLocaleString('tr-TR', ...). When an English-language user hits a sync conflict and compares Local vs Cloud timestamps (rendered at lines 156 and 183), both show Turkish month abbreviations ('Eki','Ağu','Haz') instead of English — in a high-stakes flow where the user picks which copy of their data to keep. The rest of the app derives locale from i18n.language (e.g. MemoryCard.tsx:75).
recommendation: Derive locale from i18n: const locale = (i18n.language||'tr').startsWith('tr') ? 'tr-TR' : 'en-US'; pass it to toLocaleString, matching MemoryCard.tsx:75.
notes: VERIFIED: hardcoded 'tr-TR' at ConflictResolutionDialog.tsx:98; formatDate used at lines 156 and 183 for both version timestamps. The established locale pattern at MemoryCard.tsx:75 is confirmed, so this component is genuinely inconsistent. Component already imports useTranslation (line 23) but only destructures t, not i18n. Real, user-impacting in EN; kept at medium given the high-stakes context offset by conflict frequency being low.

title: Birthday and export/chat dates use browser locale instead of app language
problem: Profile.tsx:127 formats the birthday with toLocaleDateString(undefined, ...); Aiya.tsx:93 (auto chat title date) and RelationshipSaver.tsx:174 (exported memory dates) call toLocaleDateString() with no locale. All follow browser/OS locale, not the in-app language, so a user with app=Turkish but phone=English sees '21 June' instead of '21 Haziran' (and vice versa) — a visible language mix on otherwise-localized screens.
recommendation: Pass an explicit locale derived from i18n.language to each toLocaleDateString (reuse the existing utils/dateFormat.ts helper which accepts a locale, or the MemoryCard.tsx:75 inline pattern).
notes: VERIFIED all three call sites: Profile.tsx:127 toLocaleDateString(undefined,...); Aiya.tsx:93 new Date().toLocaleDateString(); RelationshipSaver.tsx:174 new Date(memory.date).toLocaleDateString(). Real but low impact: only visible when app language and OS locale disagree (a minority), and the affected surfaces (birthday line, auto-generated chat title, plaintext export) are secondary.

title: TR/EN tone mismatch on 'breathing': imperative (TR) vs gerund (EN)
problem: breathing is 'Nefes Al' (TR imperative, i18n.ts:435) vs 'Breathing' (EN gerund, i18n.ts:1580). The two locales use different grammatical voices for the same string.
recommendation: Make the two locales consistent in voice. NOTE: the original recommendation to change EN to imperative 'Breathe' is WRONG for the actual render context — see notes.
notes: PREMISE PARTIALLY MIS-READ. The finding claims t('breathing') is 'rendered as a button/action label'. Verified at Home.tsx:494-505: it is actually shown ONLY while isBreathing is true, inside an AnimatePresence block next to a LoadingSpinner — i.e. it is a STATUS/progress label during a breathing-exercise animation, not a call-to-action button. In that context the EN gerund 'Breathing' (= 'Breathing...') is the grammatically correct form, and it is the TR imperative 'Nefes Al' that reads oddly as a status. So changing EN to 'Breathe' would make EN worse. Kept isReal:true because a genuine cross-locale voice inconsistency exists, but downgraded to low and the recommendation direction is reversed (consider 'Nefes al...' or 'Breathing'/'Breathe in' alignment). Minor.

title: dailyPrompt vs dailyQuestion: identical in TR, divergent in EN
problem: In TR both dailyPrompt (i18n.ts:408) and dailyQuestion (i18n.ts:409) are 'Günlük Soru'. In EN they diverge: dailyPrompt='Daily Prompt' (i18n.ts:1553), dailyQuestion='Daily Question' (i18n.ts:1554). Home.tsx:394 renders t('dailyPrompt'), so an EN user sees 'Daily Prompt' while a TR user sees 'Günlük Soru' (= Daily Question). 'Prompt' is more jargony than the TR 'Soru'.
recommendation: Pick one term per concept; if the header is a question, set the dailyPrompt EN value to 'Daily Question' (or consolidate the two near-duplicate keys) so EN matches the TR meaning.
notes: VERIFIED: TR dailyPrompt/dailyQuestion both 'Günlük Soru' (i18n.ts:408-409); EN diverges (1553-1554); the rendered key at Home.tsx:394 is t('dailyPrompt'). Real cross-language terminology drift, but cosmetic and subjective ('Prompt' is acceptable product English). Low.

title: memberSince key defined in both languages but never used
problem: memberSince (i18n.ts:187 'Üye: {{date}}', i18n.ts:1319 'Member since {{date}}') is defined in both locales but has no t('memberSince') call site — dead translation weight. If ever wired up, the TR phrasing 'Üye: {{date}}' reads as the grammatically-incomplete 'Member: <date>'.
recommendation: Remove the unused key, or if intended for the profile header, wire it up and reword TR to 'Üye olma tarihi: {{date}}' or 'Üyelik: {{date}}'.
notes: VERIFIED dead: grep for memberSince across src finds only the two i18n.ts definitions and zero t('memberSince') usages. No user impact whatsoever today — pure maintenance noise; the secondary point (weak TR phrasing) is only hypothetical since it never renders. Kept as a low-priority cleanup; this is the weakest item in the set.

title: At 0 remaining messages the composer stays fully enabled — user types, waits on typing dots, then gets a generic error
problem: usageInfo (Aiya.tsx:429-447) exposes used/limit but nothing gates the UI. handleSend (Aiya.tsx:878-880) only guards `if (!text || sending) return` — no `usageInfo.used >= usageInfo.limit` check. The send button is disabled only on `sending || !input.trim()` (Aiya.tsx:1426) and the textarea only on `sending` (Aiya.tsx:1419). So at exactly the cap (e.g. 50/50) the user types, hits send, sees their optimistic bubble appear (Aiya.tsx:892-899), sees TypingDots 'Aiya is typing…' (Aiya.tsx:1343), waits the full edge-function round trip (up to the 30s timeout), and only then the server 429s, the bubble is rolled back (Aiya.tsx:986-993) and the generic aiyaLimitReached toast (mapped at Aiya.tsx:978) appears. The user is led to believe a reply is coming when it never can. There is no proactive at-limit state, no disabled composer, no 'when does it reset / how to get more' affordance.
recommendation: When usageInfo.used >= usageInfo.limit, disable the textarea + send button and show a clear at-limit banner (reuse the existing t('aiyaLimitReached') string, plus reset/upgrade guidance). Short-circuit handleSend before the network call so the fake typing indicator never shows at the cap.
notes: Verified true against current code. usageInfo with used/limit exists (429-447) but is never consulted by handleSend (878-880) or the send/textarea disabled conditions (1419,1426). The wasted-round-trip + rollback flow is exactly as described. High is justified: at the cap every send is a guaranteed dead-end with misleading feedback. i18n string already exists, so the gating banner is cheap.

title: No near-limit warning — the usage bar looks identical at 49/50 and 5/50, and is absent from the chat view where messages are spent
problem: The usage indicator (Aiya.tsx:1061-1073) is a single from-primary→orange gradient bar plus a 'used/limit' count, rendered ONLY in the list header. It is not present anywhere in the chat view (chatView, Aiya.tsx:1188-1435), which is the only place messages are consumed. There is no color change or warning text as the count approaches the cap, so 48/50 reads the same as 5/50 and a user deep in a conversation can run out mid-thought with no forewarning.
recommendation: Surface the remaining count in the chat view (e.g. near the composer) and switch the bar/label to a warning tone with a short 'N left' note once used/limit crosses ~80%.
notes: Verified true — bar only in list header, no warning state, not in chat view. Downgraded high→low: this is a polish/enhancement, not a broken or blocking state. Its user impact is largely a milder version of aiya-at-limit-no-gating (which is the real fix). Worth doing alongside that finding.

title: Aiya's markdown is stripped, not rendered — list/heading prefixes leak as literal text, emphasis is destroyed
problem:
Assistant replies pass through cleanMarkdown (Aiya.tsx:124-131) before storage (applied at Aiya.tsx:951), which only removes inline emphasis markers (**, *, _, `, ~~). It does NOT touch list markers ('- ', '1. ') or headings ('## '). The bubble then renders the result as a single

with whitespace-pre-wrap (Aiya.tsx:335-337). Result a user sees: any list keeps raw '- '/'1. ' prefixes as literal text; '## Summary' renders verbatim; intended emphasis is silently flattened. For a reflective companion that returns multi-point reflection plans, structured advice becomes a hard-to-scan wall of text on mobile.
recommendation: Render assistant replies with a lightweight markdown renderer (bold, lists, line breaks, links) instead of stripping markers; at minimum convert/strip list and heading prefixes so no raw markdown leaks into the UI.
notes:
Verified true. cleanMarkdown regexes confirmed to only handle inline emphasis; list/heading prefixes pass through untouched and render literally in the pre-wrap

. Medium is fair: readability hit on the core conversational surface, but degraded-not-broken. A renderer adds a dependency (CLAUDE.md 1.17) — the minimal prefix-conversion path keeps effort lower.

title: Chats cannot be renamed — the auto-generated title (first 40 chars of the first message) is permanent
problem: The title is derived once via generateTitle from the first user message (Aiya.tsx:90-94, applied at Aiya.tsx:896) and never editable. The kebab menu offers only Delete and Close (Aiya.tsx:1240-1259). A chat that opened with 'merhaba' is forever titled 'merhaba — <date>'; a chat whose first message was a long sensitive disclosure shows that text as its permanent list headline. Users keeping many conversations cannot organize or relabel them.
recommendation: Add a Rename option to the kebab menu with an inline-editable title so users can give chats meaningful names and overwrite an awkward or sensitive auto-title.
notes: Verified true — no rename affordance anywhere; menu confirmed Delete + Close only. Genuine missing feature rather than a defect, hence low. Closely related to aiya-list-snippet-shows-raw-first-message; both are addressed by adding rename.

title: A sensitive/crisis first message becomes the chat's permanent list title in plaintext
problem: In the list each chat shows chat.title (the first user message, Aiya.tsx:1146-1148) and a snippet of the last message (Aiya.tsx:1127-1129). For a journaling app the first message may be a deeply personal or crisis disclosure, which then appears verbatim as the conversation's headline — visible to anyone glancing at the phone, and unchangeable because there is no rename (see aiya-no-rename).
recommendation: Address together with rename support; optionally default crisis-tier chats (crisisActive / route.tier==='crisis') to a neutral title and/or offer a setting to hide list previews.
notes: Mechanically verified (title=first message, snippet=last message, no rename). Real but the severity is partly speculative about content sensitivity; downgraded medium→low. It is essentially the privacy facet of aiya-no-rename and should be fixed in the same change — flagging both as separate high-impact items would over-state it.

title: No token streaming + a 30s timeout: long replies show only bouncing dots and hard-fail if generation runs long
problem: sendMessage is fully non-streamed: invokeAiya awaits the whole edge-function response wrapped in withTimeout(REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS=30000) (aiyaService.ts:48,457-461,560-581). The UI shows only the static TypingDots indicator (Aiya.tsx:1343) for the entire wait. For a deep/crisis-tier reply (full memory context, long generation) the user can stare at three dots with no progress and it reads as frozen; if generation exceeds 30s the request rejects, the user's message is rolled back (Aiya.tsx:986-993) and they see a generic network error after waiting — and the most thoughtful long replies are the most likely to time out.
recommendation: Stream tokens so long replies feel alive and partial content survives. If streaming is out of scope, add an elapsed-time hint after a few seconds and raise/clarify the timeout for deep-tier requests.
notes: Verified: non-streamed invoke, 30s timeout, static dots, rollback on failure all confirmed. Real but downgraded medium→low: streaming is a large architectural change (edge function + client), and 30s is usually sufficient, so day-to-day impact is limited. The cheap, valuable slice is the elapsed-time hint / clearer timeout copy — worth doing independent of full streaming.

title: Send-failure rollback deletes the user's bubble and re-injects text — looks like the message vanished, and a fresh draft silently discards it
problem: On any send error the optimistic user bubble is popped (Aiya.tsx:986-992) and the text restored via setInput((cur) => cur || text) (Aiya.tsx:993). From the user's POV the message they just saw in the thread suddenly disappears and reappears as draft text, with a separate red error block above — disorienting and readable as data loss, with no 'failed — tap to retry' affordance tying the restored text to the failure. Edge case: the `cur || text` guard means if the user started typing a NEW message during the in-flight send, the failed text is silently discarded (new draft wins).
recommendation: Keep the failed bubble with an inline 'failed — tap to retry' affordance instead of deleting it; at minimum make the returned-to-box behavior explicit. Handle the case where the input already holds new content so the failed message isn't lost (e.g. append, or queue a retry).
notes: Verified true: pop logic (986-992) and `cur || text` restore (993) confirmed. The silent-discard edge case is real given async send + free-typing textarea. Medium is right — failures are intermittent but when they happen the disappearing-bubble UX is genuinely confusing and the discard path loses user text without notice.

title: Crisis support banner renders inline below messages and scrolls out of view as the conversation continues; emergency number isn't tappable
problem: crisisActive is set on a crisis-tier message (Aiya.tsx:936) and reset only on new-chat/open-chat (Aiya.tsx:812,825). The banner renders inline in the message flow, after the bubble list and before TypingDots/error (Aiya.tsx:1322-1340). Consequences: (1) as the user keeps chatting, each new message pushes the safety resources further up and eventually off-screen — the 112/911 info scrolls away exactly when it should stay reachable; (2) it cannot be dismissed within a session; (3) sitting before TypingDots, on a fresh crisis message it can briefly show before Aiya's actual reply arrives. The emergency number in aiyaCrisisResources (i18n.ts:515,1647) is plain text, not a tel: link.
recommendation: Pin the crisis resources to a persistent non-scrolling spot (sticky strip above the composer) for the rest of the session, and make the emergency number a tappable tel: link where the platform allows.
notes: Verified true: crisisActive lifecycle (812,825,936) and inline placement in the scroll flow (1322-1340) confirmed; i18n resources string is plain text. Medium (not high) because the resource text is generic guidance rather than a single critical action, but for safety-relevant content a banner that scrolls away and an un-tappable emergency number are real gaps worth fixing.

title: Background profile build fails silently and the personalization it powers has zero user-facing surface
problem: maybeUpdateProfile (Aiya.tsx:855-875) fires an unmetered buildProfile after qualifying sends, wrapped in a fully silent `catch { /* silent */ }` (Aiya.tsx:874). The evolving profile summary that makes Aiya feel personalized is never shown to the user — there's no 'memory updated' affordance and no way to view or reset what Aiya has inferred. For a product whose promise is 'an assistant that knows you', the learning step has no surface, and a user whose profile build repeatedly fails would never know why Aiya doesn't seem to remember them.
recommendation: Add a small optional surface (e.g. in settings: 'What Aiya remembers about you') with a clear/reset control, so users understand and trust the personalization.
notes: Verified true: silent catch and absent UI surface confirmed. Downgraded medium→low. Note the 'invisible cost' framing is partly addressed already — the build is intentionally unmetered and the code comment (870-873) explains it deliberately does not touch the quota counter, so there is no hidden billing. The remaining real point is the missing trust/transparency surface, which is a feature gap rather than a defect.

title: On a fresh chat the centered empty-state hero and the bottom suggestion chips compete for the same 'get started' job
problem: showChips (Aiya.tsx:1186) shows chips when messages.length===0 or the last message is an assistant reply and input is empty — so on an empty new chat the large centered hero ('...you can ask questions!', Aiya.tsx:1285-1301) and the suggestion chips at the bottom (Aiya.tsx:1387-1394) render at the same time, both doing the 'start here' job. On small screens this is slightly redundant/cluttered. The finding's other half — chips hiding while a send is in flight — is the expected behavior the finding itself concedes is acceptable.
recommendation: Tighten the empty-chat layout so the hero and the suggestion chips don't duplicate the 'get started' affordance on a fresh chat (e.g. fold the chips into the hero, or drop the hero copy once chips are visible).
notes: Verified: the simultaneous hero+chips on an empty chat is real (1285-1301 and 1387-1394 both render when messages.length===0). The bulk of the finding's prose describes normal/expected chip-visibility behavior, so the actionable kernel is just the minor first-impression clutter. Low severity, cosmetic.

title: Core-memory badge uses orange in the Vault list but yellow on Home for the same status
problem: The core-memory badge renders with the orange brand gradient in MemoryCard (line 194: `bg-gradient-to-r from-primary to-primary-dark text-white`) but with a yellow gradient in Home's Random Memory panel (line 582: `from-yellow-400 to-yellow-500 text-white`). The identical '⭐ Core Memory' chip therefore has two visual identities depending on screen, weakening the meaning of 'core'. Note the codebase is already inconsistent on yellow vs orange for this concept: Home also uses `text-yellow-500` for the core star in Quick Stats (line 707) and the On-This-Day card (line 860), while MemoryCard uses orange — so this is a genuine cross-screen inconsistency.
recommendation: Pick one canonical core-memory color (the star glyph implies gold/yellow) and apply it to both the MemoryCard badge and the Home Random Memory badge so the status reads as one concept everywhere.
notes: Verified exact lines. MemoryCard.tsx:194 orange gradient; Home.tsx:582 yellow gradient. Confirmed real cross-screen divergence. Cosmetic but user-perceptible; medium is fair.

title: Recharts pie slice labels have no dark-mode fill, rendering low-contrast on dark cards
problem: The two PieCharts pass `label` as a plain string callback (lines 368-373 and 429-434) with no fill, so recharts draws the percent/name labels with its default SVG text fill (mid-gray, ~#808080). The bar/line axis ticks explicitly fix this with `tick={{ className: 'fill-gray-500 dark:fill-gray-400 ...' }}` (lines 341-342, 402-403), but the pie labels get no theme-aware treatment. On the dark card surface (`dark:bg-gray-800`) the category and life-area pie labels are low-contrast gray-on-dark-gray. The chart container also has no text-color class to inherit from.
recommendation: Render the pie label via a custom label component using `fill='currentColor'` (and set a theme-aware text color on the container), or pass an explicit `fill` that adapts to dark mode, so the percentages/names stay legible on dark backgrounds.
notes: Confirmed pie labels get no fill and no wrapping text color. The finding's 'near-black/unreadable' is overstated — recharts default is mid-gray (~#808080), which is low-contrast (fails WCAG) on gray-800 but not invisible. Downgraded high->medium.

title: Chart tooltip shows a bare number with no category/series name
problem: CustomTooltip (lines 39-49) renders only `entry.value` per payload item plus an optional axis `label`. PieCharts pass no axis label, so hovering a category/life-area slice shows just the count (e.g. '4') with no indication of which slice. For the intensity/monthly bar charts the y-value alone is shown. The slice name is available in the payload but is not rendered.
recommendation: Include the series/category name in the tooltip (e.g. `${entry.name}: ${entry.value}`). For pies the name comes from `payload[0].name`.
notes: Verified CustomTooltip renders only entry.value (line 45) and pies pass no label. Real but low impact — slices are color-coded and labeled directly on the pie, so the tooltip is supplementary. Downgraded medium->low.

title: Success splash checkmark uses text-green-500, not the app's success token
problem: The success theme color is #10B981 (tailwind.config.js:18-20, success.DEFAULT; also the toast success icon in Toaster.tsx:23). The full-screen SuccessAnimation checkmark uses `text-green-500` (#22C55E) at line 53 — a brighter green. SuccessAnimation is actually used (Vault.tsx imports and renders it on save/bulk actions), so a save can show a #10B981 toast and a #22C55E splash that are subtly mismatched.
recommendation: Use `text-success` for the SuccessAnimation checkmark so it matches the toast icon and the design token.
notes: Confirmed tailwind success.DEFAULT=#10B981, SuccessAnimation uses text-green-500 (#22C55E), and SuccessAnimation is rendered in Vault.tsx (lines 274-277). Real but purely cosmetic; low.

title: Profile streak stat tile looks tappable like its siblings but is an inert div
problem: The three quick-stat tiles share identical card styling, but Memories (line 253) and Connections (line 283) are `<button>`s that navigate and have `hover:border-primary/40`, while the middle Streak tile (line 271) is a plain `<div>` with no onClick and no hover-border. A user who taps Memories then taps the adjacent Streak tile expecting a drill-in gets nothing, with no visual cue that this one tile is non-interactive.
recommendation: Either make the streak tile navigate somewhere meaningful (e.g. /statistics) for parity, or visually differentiate it (drop the implicit-affordance styling) so users don't expect a tap target.
notes: Verified: Profile.tsx lines 253/283 are buttons with hover:border-primary/40 and navigate; line 271 is a div with neither. Real affordance inconsistency.

title: ProgressiveImage 'blur-up' placeholder is a flat gray rect, not a real LQIP
problem: ProgressiveImage is documented as a blur-up image (lines 18-25) but, absent a caller-supplied `placeholder`, falls back to DEFAULT_PLACEHOLDER — a solid #e5e7eb SVG rect (lines 15-16) shown with `blur-sm` (line 67). MemoryCard passes no placeholder (lines 242-247), so every photo in the grid shows a uniform gray box that cross-fades to the full image. On slow connections this is a gray flash with no preview of the incoming photo, i.e. not true blur-up.
recommendation: Either generate/store a tiny base64 LQIP and pass it as `placeholder`, or relabel this as a simple gray-placeholder fade. At minimum add a subtle shimmer so the box reads as loading rather than static.
notes: Verified DEFAULT_PLACEHOLDER is a flat gray SVG and MemoryCard passes no placeholder. Real but expected-behavior/polish, not a defect; an actual LQIP needs pipeline work (medium). Low severity is right.

title: Random-memory image error fallback double-encodes the data URI, breaking the placeholder SVG
problem: The Random Memory onError handler (lines 565-570) builds `'data:image/svg+xml,' + encodeURIComponent('<svg ... fill="%23e5e7eb" ... fill="%239ca3af" ...>📷</text></svg>')`. The SVG string already contains pre-encoded `%23` color entities, then the whole string is run through encodeURIComponent again, turning `%23` into `%2523`. The browser decodes that to literal `%23e5e7eb`/`%239ca3af` as color values, which are invalid, so the intended gray '📷' fallback fails to render and the user sees the browser's broken-image glyph when a memory photo fails to load. The `%` in `50%`/`.3em` etc. are also affected.
recommendation: Don't double-encode: build the SVG with literal `#` characters and a single encodeURIComponent pass, or use the already-encoded string verbatim without wrapping it. Mirror the (correct) ProgressiveImage error path used in MemoryCard.
notes: Confirmed empirically with node: encodeURIComponent of the source string produces `%2523e5e7eb` (double-encoded). The fill values become invalid so the fallback rect/text won't render as intended. Genuine bug; medium since it only surfaces on a photo load failure (edge case).

title: Synced-but-uncategorized card pulses 'Aiya classifying...' indefinitely with no terminal/failure state
problem: The category chip pulses 'Aiya kategorize ediyor...' whenever `memory.category === 'uncategorized' && !isSyncStale && !isLocalUser` (lines 256-266). `isSyncStale` is only ever true for UNSYNCED memories older than 5 min (lines 90-95: `if (memory.synced) return false`). So for a memory that is synced but never got categorized (rate limit, rejected request, offline edge fn), `isSyncStale` stays false forever and the chip pulses 'classifying...' indefinitely with no failure state and no way to retry.
recommendation: Add a terminal state for synced uncategorized memories: after a reasonable elapsed time since createdAt (or on a known failure flag), stop the pulse and show a static 'Uncategorized' or a tap-to-retry chip instead of an endless 'classifying' animation.
notes: Verified the pulse condition and that isSyncStale returns false for any synced memory, so the synced-uncategorized case has no timeout. The unsynced case does self-terminate after 5 min via isSyncStale. Real for the synced path described in the finding.
